laws.title: Amendment of Subsection C (Authority to Recover Costs)
laws.content:
Subsection 3-2-6(C) of the Grangeville Municipal Code is hereby amended to add the following new paragraphs:

**6. Motor Vehicle Accidents.** The city shall have the authority to charge and recover from the responsible party the actual costs incurred by the city for providing emergency response services in connection with a motor vehicle accident, including but not limited to vehicle fires, extrication, fluid spill cleanup, debris removal, scene safety, and traffic control. For vehicle fires, the owner of the vehicle shall be the responsible party unless another person is determined to have caused the fire, in which case such other person shall be the responsible party.

**7. Traffic Control.** The city shall have the authority to charge and recover from the responsible party the actual costs incurred by the city for providing traffic control services in connection with any emergency incident.

**8. Hazardous Materials Response.** The city shall have the authority to charge and recover from the responsible party the actual costs incurred by the city for responding to and mitigating hazardous materials incidents. For hazardous substance incidents as defined in Idaho Code, the city shall submit documented costs to the Idaho Office of Emergency Management within sixty (60) days after the incident commander declares the incident terminated, for cost recovery in accordance with Idaho Code. For other hazardous materials incidents not meeting that statutory definition, including routine vehicle fluid spills and minor releases, the city may pursue cost recovery directly under this section.

**9. Mutual Aid Response for Real Property.** Pursuant to Idaho Code, the city shall have the authority to charge and recover reasonable fees from the owner of real property located outside the corporate limits of the city for fire suppression, emergency medical, rescue, hazardous materials response, or other emergency services provided by the fire department to such property.

**10. Insurance Claims.** The city may file claims for cost recovery directly with the responsible party’s insurance carrier. The responsible party shall provide insurance information upon request. The city may utilize third-party billing services to pursue cost recovery.

**11. General Authority.** The authority to recover costs under this section applies regardless of whether the responsible party or property owner requested such services.

**12. Multiple Responsible Parties.** Where an incident involves multiple responsible parties, each responsible party shall be jointly and severally liable for the full amount of actual costs incurred. The city may pursue cost recovery against any or all responsible parties, in any amount, until the full costs have been recovered.

laws.title: Amendment of Subsection D (Determination of Costs)
laws.content:
Subsection 3-2-6(D) of the Grangeville Municipal Code is hereby amended to add the following new paragraph:

**3. Fee Schedule.** The rates charged for emergency response services shall be as follows:

b. Personnel costs shall be based on actual hourly wages plus benefits; and

c. Consumable supplies, materials, and specialized equipment shall be charged at actual cost.

SECTION 6. Amendment of Subsection G (Collection of Unpaid Bills).

Subsection 3-2-6(G) of the Grangeville Municipal Code is hereby amended to add the following new paragraph:

4. Lien for Mutual Aid Responses. For mutual aid responses to real property located outside the corporate limits of the city, the city shall have a lien upon the property serviced. The lien claim shall be filed with the county recorder within ninety (90) days after completion of services, shall contain the information required by Idaho Code, and shall be served on the property owner by certified mail within five (5) business days of filing. Any action to foreclose the lien shall be commenced within six (6) months of the lien filing date.

SECTION 7. Amendment of Subsection H (Exemptions).

Subsection 3-2-6(H) of the Grangeville Municipal Code is hereby amended to add the following new paragraphs to Subsection H(1):

d. Motor vehicle accidents in which the owner of a vehicle was injured or suffered property damage caused by the fault of another party, provided that nothing in this exemption shall relieve a vehicle owner of responsibility for costs incurred in response to a fire involving the owner’s own vehicle unless another party is determined to be at fault for causing such fire; hazardous materials incidents or traffic control incidents caused solely by natural disasters or circumstances beyond the control of any identifiable responsible party, as determined by the fire chief;

e. Mutual aid responses where reimbursement is provided by another governmental entity pursuant to a mutual aid agreement.

SECTION 8. Severability.

If any section, subsection, sentence, clause, phrase, or portion of this ordinance is for any reason held invalid or unconstitutional by any court of competent jurisdiction, such portion shall be deemed a separate, distinct, and independent provision and such holding shall not affect the validity of the remaining portions of this ordinance.

SECTION 9. Effective Date.

This ordinance shall become effective upon its passage, approval, and publication in the Idaho County Free Press.

This ordinance passed under a suspension of the rule requiring three readings on separate days held at a regular meeting of the City Council on the 15th day of December, 2025.

WES LESTER, Mayor

ATTEST:

TONYA KENNEDY, City Clerk

laws.title: Title 8, Chapter 5 of the Grangeville Municipal Code is hereby amended by adding 8-5-6 subsection G4
laws.content:
8-5-6 G4 : WATER METERS FOR MOBILE HOME PARKS, MANUFACTURED HOME PARKS, AND RECREATIONAL VEHICLE PARKS.

Each park shall be served by one (1) water meter. Where a park’s size, topography, or layout requires additional service connections to meet applicable plumbing and public drinking water standards, the Public Works Director may approve one (1) additional meter per required pressure zone. The number of meters shall not exceed the minimum required under applicable standards, as determined by the Public Works Director. Individual meters for individual lots, spaces, or units within a park are prohibited regardless of park size or configuration.

If any provision of this Ordinance or its application to any person or circumstance is held invalid, the remainder of the Ordinance and the application of its provisions to other persons or circumstances shall not be affected.

This ordinance passed under a suspension of the rule requiring three readings on separate days held at a regular meeting of the City Council on the 2nd day of March, 2026.

Wes Lester, Mayor

laws.title: Effect of Repealing Ordinances
laws.content: The repeal of ordinances as provided shall not affect any right which has accrued, any duty imposed, any penalty incurred, nor any action or proceedings as commenced under or by virtue of the ordinances repealed, nor the tenure of office of any person holding office at the time when such ordinances take effect; nor shall the repeal of any ordinance thereby have the effect of reviving any ordinance therefor repealed or superseded. (1959 Code)

laws.title: Rules for Construction
laws.content:
In the construction of the official Code and all ordinances amendatory thereof or supplementary thereto the following rules shall be observed unless such construction would be inconsistent with the manifest intent of the legislative body or repugnant to the context.

A. Intent To Defraud: Whenever, by any of the provisions of the official Code, an intent to defraud is required in order to constitute an offense, it is sufficient if an intent appears to defraud any person, association or body politic or any combination of persons.

B. Liability Of Employers And Agents: When the provision herein contained prohibits the commission or omission of an act, not only the person actually doing the prohibited thing or omitting the directed act, but also the employer and all other persons concerned or aiding or abetting the person shall be guilty of the offense described and liable to the penalty set forth.

C. Title Of Sections And Subsections: The title of any section or subsection of this official Code shall be deemed in nowise to restrict, qualify or to limit the effect of the provisions set forth and contained in such section or subsection.

D. Constitutionality; Effect Of: Should any portion of this official Code be declared by any court of competent jurisdiction to be unconstitutional or void, such adjudication shall in no way affect the remaining portion of this Code. (1959 Code)

laws.title: Corporate Seal
laws.content:
A. Design: The Corporate Seal of the City of Grangeville shall be circular in form with inner and outer circles. The outer circle shall be two inches (2") in diameter, and the inner circle one and one-fourth inches (1 1/4") in diameter. It shall bear upon the space between the two (2) circles the words, "Grangeville, Idaho, Idaho County", and upon the space within the inner circle the words, "Incorporated October, 1897", and the word "SEAL", as follows:

![image](image_1.png)

B. Adoption: The Seal described in the above Section of this Chapter be and the same is hereby adopted as the Corporate Seal of the City of Grangeville, Idaho. (1959 Code)

laws.title: Municipal Depositories
laws.content:
A. Designated: The Bank of Central Idaho, Grangeville, Idaho, and the First Security Bank of Idaho, Grangeville Branch, N.A., Grangeville, Idaho, are hereby designated as the official depositories for Municipal funds. (Ord. 324, 6-11-1959)

B. Demand Funds: Pursuant to Idaho Code 50-1013, the City Clerk/Treasurer be and is hereby authorized to deposit all demand funds of the City in such qualified depository or depositories as defined by Idaho Code title 57, chapter 1, as shall be determined by the City Council by competitive bidding or other means generally accepted as a standard business practice, all as authorized by Idaho Code 57-128.

Prior to and until a depository or depositories shall be designated by the City Council, pursuant to Idaho Code 57-128, the City Clerk/Treasurer be and is hereby authorized to continue the existing practice of keeping City money deposited with each designated depository within the City or within Idaho County in such proportion of the total deposits of the City as capital and the surplus of each depository bears to the total capital and surplus of all designated depositories within the City or Idaho County. (Ord. 564, 7-7-1983)

laws.title: City Elections; Voting Hours
laws.content: Pursuant to the provisions of Idaho Code 50-453 as amended, the polls at all general and special City elections shall be opened at twelve o'clock (12:00) noon on election day and remain open until all registered voters of that precinct have voted or until eight o'clock (8:00) P.M. of the same day, whichever occurs first. (Ord. 703, 8-18-1997)

laws.title: General Penalty
laws.content: Any person convicted of a violation of any section of this Code shall be fined as established in the master fee schedule for any one offense, and such person may be confined in the Municipal Jail for a period of not more than thirty (30) days. Either or both such fine and imprisonment may be imposed. (Ord. 349, 12-4-1961; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018)

laws.title: Default
laws.content: Any person in default of payment of any fine imposed shall be imprisoned in the Municipal Jail for a period of one day for each five dollars ($5.00) of such fine. (1959 Code)

laws.title: Driving While Intoxicated
laws.content: Any person convicted of driving a motor vehicle while intoxicated or under the influence of intoxicating liquor or narcotic drugs shall be fined in the amount as established in the master fee schedule and may also be confined in the Municipal Jail for not more than thirty (30) days; provided, that upon conviction, said person shall also surrender his driver’s license to the court. (1959 Code; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018)

laws.title: Labor
laws.content: Any person imprisoned under the provisions of this chapter may be put to work for the benefit of the City for the term of his imprisonment. No female prisoner shall be required to work in public, nor shall any prisoner be required to work on Sunday. (1959 Code)

laws.title: Public Records
laws.content:
**SECTION:**

1-11-1: Definitions

1-11-2: Public Records; Public Access

1-11-3: Response To Request For Public Access

1-11-4: Appeal Of Denial To Public Records

1-11-5: Exempt Records

**1-11-1: DEFINITIONS:**

CITY: City of Grangeville.

CUSTODIAN: The person having personal custody and control of the public records and shall refer to the City Clerk and his or her designee.

EXEMPT: The custodian is free from the obligation to disclose public records.

INSPECT: The right to listen, view, and make notes of public records as long as the public record is not altered or damaged.

PUBLIC RECORD: Includes, but is not limited to, any writing containing information relating to the conduct or administration of the public’s business prepared, owned, used or retained by the City regardless of physical form or characteristics.

WRITING: Includes, but is not limited to, hand writing, type writing, printing, photostating, photographing, and every means of recording, including letters, words, pictures, sounds or symbols, or combination thereof, and all papers, maps, magnetic or paper tapes, photographic films and prints, magnetic or punched cards, discs, drums or other documents. (Ord. 633, 10-21-1991)

**1-11-2: PUBLIC RECORDS; PUBLIC ACCESS:**

All public records of the City shall be open and available to the general public during the hours of nine o’clock (9:00) A.M. to eleven forty five o’clock (11:45) A.M. and one fifteen o’clock (1:15) P.M. through four thirty o’clock (4:30) P.M. Monday through Friday, except declared holidays.

Any individual seeking public records shall make their request to the custodian, or his designee, during the above stated hours. Every individual shall have the right to inspect and every effort will be made to facilitate this right. However, nothing shall prevent the custodian from maintaining such vigilance to prevent alteration of any public record. A written request will be required if the record desired is not readily available or identifiable by the custodian, or his designee. (Ord. 633, 10-21-1991)

Any individual seeking copies of public records may utilize their own equipment, however, public records shall not be removed from City Hall. Copies of public records may be made upon City copying equipment at a rate as established in the master fee schedule. (Ord. 633, 10-21-1991; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018)

Public records may be inspected outside of the above stated hours if requested in writing with said request being made in advance. The person requesting said inspection will be responsible for compensation to the City at the cost of said inspection.

Where it is in the public interest to do so, the Mayor, any City Council member, or any supervisory employee, or the custodian may waive any fee required in this Chapter. (Ord. 633, 10-21-1991)

**1-11-3: RESPONSE TO REQUEST FOR PUBLIC ACCESS:**

Every individual seeking to inspect the public record shall either be granted or denied the right within three (3) working days of the request. If the custodian determines that more time is needed to locate or retrieve the public records, the custodian shall notify the person requesting to inspect the public records of said delay, in writing. In no event shall the delay extend later than ten (10) working days.

If the custodian fails to respond to the request it shall be deemed denied within ten (10) working days following the request or if the request is deemed denied then notice of denial will be reviewed by the City Attorney and shall state the statutory authority for the denial and indicate the person’s right to appeal the denial. (Ord. 633, 10-21-1991)

**1-11-4: APPEAL OF DENIAL TO PUBLIC RECORDS:**

Any individual aggrieved by the denial of a request for disclosure of public records may institute proceeding in District Court to compel the City to make the records available pursuant to law. (Ord. 633, 10-21-1991)

**1-11-5: EXEMPT RECORDS:**

The following records are exempt from disclosure:

A. Any public record exempt from disclosure by Federal or State law or Federal regulations to the extent specifically provided for by such law or regulation.

B. Production records, sale or purchase records, cash records, mortgage portfolio loan documents, or similar business records of a private concern or enterprise required by law to be submitted to or inspected by a public agency. Nothing in this subsection shall limit the use which can be made of such information for regulatory purposes or its admissibility in any enforcement proceeding.

C. Records relating to the appraisal of real property, timber, or mineral rights prior to its acquisition, sale or lease by a public agency.

D. Any estimate prepared by a public agency that details the cost of a public project until such time as disclosed or bids are opened, or upon award of the contract for construction of the public project.

E. Test questions, scoring keys, and other data used to administer a licensing examination, employment, academic or other examination or testing procedure before the examination is given if the examination is to be used again. Records establishing procedures for and instructing persons administering, grading or evaluating an examination or testing procedure are included in this exemption, to the extent that disclosure would create a risk that the result might be affected.

F. Retired employees’ and retired public officials’ home addresses, home telephone numbers and other financial and nonfinancial membership records; active employee financial and membership records and mortgage portfolio loan documents maintained by the public employee retirement system. Financial statements prepared by retirement system staff, funding agents and custodians concerning the investment of assets of the public employee retirement system of Idaho are not considered confidential under this Chapter.

G. Any personal records, other than names and addresses, such as parentage, race, religion, sex, height, weight, tax identification and social security numbers, financial worth or medical condition submitted to any public agency pursuant to a statutory requirement for licensing, certification, permit or bonding.
H. Unless otherwise provided by agency rule, information obtained as part of any inquiry into a person’s fitness to be granted or retain a license, certificate, permit, privilege, commission or position.

I. Employment security information and unemployment insurance benefit information, except that all interested parties may agree to waive the exemption.

J. Investigatory records of a law enforcement agency, as defined in Idaho Code 9-337(5), under the conditions set forth in Idaho Code 9-335.

K. Records of a personal nature related directly or indirectly to the application for and provision of statutory services rendered to persons applying for public care for the elderly, indigent, or mentally or physically handicapped, or participation in an environmental or a public health study.

L. Records of hospital care, medical records, records of psychiatric care or treatment and professional counseling records relating to an individual’s condition, diagnosis, care or treatment.

M. Records of a person maintained pursuant to Idaho Code, title 16, chapter 18.

N. Except as provided in this subsection, all personnel records of a current or former public official other than the public official’s public service or employment history, classification, pay grade and step, longevity, gross salary and salary history, status, workplace and employing agency. All other personnel information relating to a public employee or applicant, including, but not limited to, information regarding sex, race, marital status, birth date, home address and telephone number, applications, testing and scoring materials, grievances, correspondence and performance evaluations, shall not be disclosed to the public without the employee’s or applicant’s written consent. A public official or authorized representative may inspect and copy his personnel records, except for material used to screen and test for employment.

O. Written communications between the City Attorney and the Mayor, City Council members and department heads when such records constitute communications within the scope of the attorney-client relationship.

P. Any written agendas, information sheets, handouts, notes or minutes of duly authorized executive meetings of the City Council. (Ord. 633, 10-21-1991)

laws.title: Library Board
laws.content:
**SECTION:**

2-2-1: Library, Creation

2-2-2: Board Appointment And Term

2-2-3: Rules; Elect Officers

2-2-4: Use Of Library Room

2-2-5: Reports Of Board

2-2-6: Donations For Library

2-2-7: Funds For Operation

2-2-8: Removal Of Library Trustees

2-2-9: Fee For Nonresident Use

2-2-10: Library Operational Fees

2-2-1: LIBRARY, CREATION:

A public library and reading room is hereby established under and by virtue of the provisions of this chapter. (1959 Code)

2-2-2: BOARD APPOINTMENT AND TERM:

Library trustees shall be appointed and serve terms pursuant to Title 33, Chapter 26, Idaho Code. (Ord. 486, 12-20-1976; amd. Ord. 974, 1-2-2024)

2-2-3: RULES; ELECT OFFICERS:

Said trustees shall immediately after their appointment, meet and organize, by the election of one of their members as president and by the election of such officers as they shall deem necessary. They shall make and adopt such rules, bylaws and regulations for their own guidance and for the government of the library and the reading room as may be expedient. The city council shall have the final control of the expenditures and all monies collected for the library fund, but the library board shall advise and recommend to the city council, which expenditures from time to time shall be appropriate and necessary for the care and custody of the library or any necessary function of the library.

The library board, subject to the approval of the city council may appoint a librarian and such other assistants as shall be deemed necessary and prescribe rules for their conduct. (Ord. 574, 5-7-1984)

2-2-4: USE OF LIBRARY ROOM:

The library and reading room hereby established shall be forever free for the use of the inhabitants of the city; always subject to such reasonable rules and regulations as the library board may find necessary to adopt and publish in order to render the use of the library and reading room of the greatest benefit to the greatest number and they may exclude and cut off from the use of said library and reading room any and all persons who shall wilfully violate such rules. (1959 Code)

2-2-5: REPORTS OF BOARD:

Said board of trustees, or their designee, shall make a quarterly report at the first meeting of the city council in the months of May, August, November and February of each year to summarize the activities of the library in the last quarter with such other statistics and information and suggestions as it may deem of general interest and the City Council may require. (1959 Code; amd. Ord. 486, 12-20-1976; Ord. 974, 1-2-2024)
2-2-6: DONATIONS FOR LIBRARY:

All persons desirous of making donations of money, personal property, or real estate for the benefit of the library may vest title to the same in the City, to be controlled by the City Council, under the advice and recommendation of the Library Board.

A. Should any donation to the library, be specific as to how such donation should be used, the City Council shall be bound by those specific restrictions.

B. In the event a donation is granted to the library without specific directions, the same shall be separately accounted for in a fund to be known as the Library Memorial Fund. Such fund may be used by the City Council with the advice and recommendation of the board for the purchase of books, magazines, or equipment, or any other capital improvement other than items required for the normal operation of the library, and shall not be used for salaries. (Ord. 573, 5-7-1984)

2-2-7: FUNDS FOR OPERATION:

There is hereby created a special fund to be known as the Library Fund, which shall be kept by the City Treasurer separate and apart from other monies of the City to be used exclusively for the purchase of books, periodicals, necessary furniture and fixtures and compensation for a librarian and assistant and whatever is required for the maintenance of such library and reading room and all monies for the use and benefit of said library shall be kept in said Library Fund. (1959 Code)

2-2-8: REMOVAL OF LIBRARY TRUSTEES:

Removal of library trustees shall be conducted pursuant to Title 33, Chapter 26, Idaho Code. (1959 Code; amd. Ord. 974, 1-2-2024)

2-2-9: FEE FOR NONRESIDENT USE:

The City Council shall have the right to fix a fee for the use of the Grangeville Municipal Library by nonresidents. Such fee for nonresident use shall be as established in the master fee schedule. Such fee as now adopted, or as shall be hereafter amended, shall entitle the card holder to one full year of library use beginning on the date of issuance and continuing for one full year thereafter. Upon the purchase of such nonresident family library card, that family shall be entitled to use the Grangeville Municipal Library in the same manner as City residents might or could do. A library card shall bear on its face its expiration date and may be renewed for the next full year after payment of the fee as established in the master fee schedule. (Ord. 742, 10-22-2001; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018)

The library staff shall maintain accurate records reflecting the issuance of each nonresident family library card as from time to time may be issued or renewed.

All receipts received by the library on account of such nonresident library card shall be kept by the City Clerk in the Library Fund pursuant to section 2-7 of this chapter.

A “nonresident” shall be defined as any person and his or her family maintaining his or her usual place of abode outside of the incorporated limits of the City. However, in the event such person living outside of the incorporated limits owns property within the City limits he or she would be considered a resident. It shall be the responsibility of any property owner claiming residency under this definition to provide adequate proof to the Library Director as to property ownership within the City. (Ord. 742, 10-22-2001)

2-2-10: LIBRARY OPERATIONAL FEES:

Library operational fees charged to the public shall be as established in the master fee schedule. (Ord. 733, 4-2-2001; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018)

laws.title: Recreation Commission
laws.content:
SECTION:

2-3-1: Establishment; Term Of Office

2-3-2: Rules And Regulations

2-3-3: Annual Budget

2-3-4: Reports

2-3-5: Advisory Commission Only

2-3-1: ESTABLISHMENT; TERM OF OFFICE:

There is hereby created a Recreation Commission for the City. The Commission shall consist of four (4) members who shall receive no salary. They shall be appointed by the Mayor and confirmed by the City Council. The members shall be chosen from the residents of the City. The term of office of each member shall be for a term of two (2) years or until his successor is appointed and qualified. Vacancies in such Commission occurring otherwise than by expiration of the term shall be filled by the Mayor for the unexpired term. (1959 Code)

2-3-2: RULES AND REGULATIONS:

Immediately after the appointment of the members of the Recreation Commission they shall meet and organize by electing one of their members president and such other officers as may be necessary. The Commission shall have the power to adopt bylaws, rules and regulations for the proper conduct of the public parks and recreation in and for the City. Said bylaws, rules and regulations are subject to the approval of the Mayor and City Council.

The Recreation Commission shall provide conduct of and the supervision of public parks and public playgrounds, athletic fields, recreation centers, recreational facilities and other recreation activities on any of the properties owned or controlled by the City, or on other properties with the consent of the owners and occupants thereof. It shall have the power to conduct any form of recreation or cultural activities that will employ the leisure time of the people in a constructive and wholesome manner.

The Recreation Commission shall have the power to appoint or designate someone to act as Superintendent, who is trained and properly qualified for the work and such other personnel as the Commission deems proper, subject to the approval of the Mayor and City Council. (1959 Code)

2-3-3: ANNUAL BUDGET:

The Recreation Commission shall submit annually a budget to the Mayor and Council of the City for their approval. The Commission may also solicit or receive any gifts or bequests of money, or other personal property or any donation, principal or income, for either temporary or permanent use for public playgrounds or other recreational purposes. Said property and/or gifts, however, to be and remain the property of the City. (1959 Code)

2-3-4: REPORTS:

The Recreation Commission shall make full and complete monthly and annual reports to the Mayor and Council of the City and other reports from time to time as requested by the Mayor and City Council. (1959 Code)

2-3-5: ADVISORY COMMISSION ONLY:

The Recreation Commission shall not be deemed to be other than an advisory commission to advise the Mayor and City Council. (1959 Code)

laws.title: Fire Department
laws.content:
SECTION: 3-2-1: Department Created 3-2-2: Fire Chief 3-2-3: Departmental Duties 3-2-4: Fire Prevention 3-2-5: Volunteer Members 3-2-6: Fire Suppression And Protection Services 3-2-1: DEPARTMENT CREATED: There is hereby created a Fire Department which shall consist of a Fire Chief and such other personnel as may be provided for by the governing body of the City. (1959 Code) 3-2-2: FIRE CHIEF: A. Appointment: The Chief of the Fire Department shall be appointed by the Mayor subject to the approval of the City Council. He shall hold office for the duration of his appointment unless sooner removed by the Mayor with the concurrence of the City Council. B. Rank: The Chief of the Fire Department, commonly referred to as the Fire Chief, shall be the head of the Department and have supervision over all officers and members thereof. The Fire Chief may, with the approval of the Mayor, appoint such other Fire Department officers as may be deemed necessary, including a First Assistant Chief and a Second Assistant Chief. C. Duties: The Fire Chief shall keep such records and make such reports concerning the activities of his Department as may be required by statute or by the Mayor. He shall be responsible for the performance of the Fire Department and of its functions and all persons who are members of the Fire Department shall serve subject to his orders. He shall be responsible for the control and custody of all Fire Department property and equipment. He shall have the authority of a police officer while actively engaged in fighting a fire, or going to or from a fire. (1959 Code) 3-2-3: DEPARTMENTAL DUTIES: It shall be the duty of members of the Fire Department to provide for the immediate answering of all fire calls and to fight all fires in the best and most modern available methods. Members shall see to the care and maintenance of all fire fighting equipment and have such equipment in constant workable condition at all times. (1959 Code) 3-2-4: FIRE PREVENTION: Every possible action shall be taken by the members of the Fire Department to eliminate fire hazards and to provide for fire prevention methods and operations within the City. (1959 Code) 3-2-5: VOLUNTEER MEMBERS: Any volunteer members of the Fire Department shall conduct themselves in the same manner and under the same rules and regulations as regular members of the Department. They shall respond to all fire calls according to a schedule prescribed by the Chief of the Fire Department and they shall attend all meetings and drills called by the Chief. (1959 Code) 3-2-6: FIRE SUPPRESSION AND PROTECTION SERVICES: A. Purpose And Intent: The purpose of this section is to establish the authority for the City of Grangeville to recover the actual costs incurred by the city in providing fire suppression and protection services in response to personal property fires within the city limits, and to recover costs associated with responding to false alarms. The intent of this section is to promote public safety, reduce the number of false alarms, and ensure that those who benefit from or necessitate fire department services bear an appropriate portion of the costs of providing such services. B. Definitions: For the purposes of this chapter, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:
ACTUAL COSTS: All costs, direct and indirect, incurred by the City of Grangeville in response to a personal property fire or false alarm. These0 costs include, but are not limited to: personnel costs (including overtime), operational costs, costs for the use of materials, equipment costs (including damage, repair, and replacement), administrative costs, and other reasonable expenses attributable to the fire response or false alarm response.
FALSE ALARM: The activation of a fire alarm system resulting in the response of the fire department when no actual fire or emergency exists. This includes activation caused by mechanical failure, malfunction, improper installation, lack of proper maintenance, negligent activation by the owner or occupant, or any other activation not caused by a fire or other emergency requiring response by the fire department.
FIRE DEPARTMENT: The Grangeville volunteer fire department or any other fire department providing services on behalf of the City of Grangeville.
FIRE CHIEF: The fire chief of the City of Grangeville or their designee.
OWNER: Any person, agent, firm, corporation, or entity having a legal or equitable interest in personal property on which fire suppression services were provided or to which the fire department responded due to a false alarm.
PERSONAL PROPERTY: Any movable or intangible property that is subject to ownership, including but not limited to vehicles, equipment, and other similar items.
C. Authority To Recover Costs: 1. The City of Grangeville shall have the authority to charge and recover from the owner of any personal property the actual costs incurred by the city for providing fire suppression and protection services in response to a fire on such personal property. 2. The city shall have the authority to charge and recover from the owner of any property the actual costs incurred by the city for responding to false alarms originating from such property, subject to the limitations set forth in section 3(D) of this chapter. 3. This authority applies regardless of whether the owner of the personal property requested such services. 4. For false alarms, the following schedule of charges shall apply: a. First through fourth false alarm within a calendar year: written warning, no charge. b. Fifth and subsequent false alarms within a calendar year: Actual costs incurred, plus an administrative fee as established in the master fee schedule. 5. The city’s authority to recover costs under this section is in addition to any other remedies available to the city under state and local law. D. Determination Of Costs: 1. The fire chief shall be responsible for determining the actual costs incurred in responding to a personal property fire. 2. The determination shall be based on actual expenses incurred, including but not limited to: a. Personnel costs, including regular and overtime wages, benefits, and workers’ compensation; b. Equipment costs, based on hourly rates established by the city or FEMA schedule of equipment rates, whichever is greater; c. Cost of materials and supplies used, damaged, or destroyed; d. Administrative costs associated with the incident and cost recovery; e. Any specialized services required, including but not limited to hazardous materials response, technical rescue, or mutual aid; and f. Any other reasonable costs attributable to the fire response. 3. The fire chief shall maintain detailed records of all costs associated with each fire response. E. Billing Procedures: 1. Within sixty (60) days after the conclusion of a personal property fire incident, the city shall send an itemized bill to the owner of the personal property, detailing the actual costs incurred for fire suppression services. 2. The bill shall include: a. The date, time, and location of the personal property fire; b. A detailed itemization of all costs being charged; c. The total amount due; d. Payment terms and due date; e. Information regarding the process for appealing the bill; and d. Contact information for questions regarding the bill. 3. Payment shall be due within thirty (30) days from the date of the invoice. F. Appeals Process: 1. Any personal property owner who wishes to contest a bill for actual costs may file a written appeal with the city clerk within fifteen (15) days of receiving the bill. 2. The appeal shall state the specific grounds upon which the bill is contested and include any supporting documentation. 3. The city council shall consider the appeal at a regular meeting within forty-five (45) days of receipt of the appeal. The property owner shall be notified of the date, time, and location of the meeting at which the appeal will be considered. 4. The city council’s decision on the appeal shall be final. G. Collection Of Unpaid Bills: 1. If a personal property owner fails to pay the bill for actual costs within thirty (30) days of the due date, and has not filed an appeal, the bill shall be considered delinquent. 2. The city may pursue any and all legal remedies to collect delinquent bills, including but not limited to: a. Referral to a collection agency; b. Filing a civil action in a court of competent jurisdiction; 3. In addition to the actual costs, the property owner shall be responsible for any interest, penalties, and collection costs associated with a delinquent bill. H. Exemptions: 1. The following are exempt from the provisions of this section relating to personal property fire suppression cost recovery: a. Fires caused by natural disasters such as lightning strikes, earthquakes, or other acts of God, unless exacerbated by the negligence of the property owner; b. Fires occurring on personal property owned by the City of Grangeville; and c. Fires that spread to a property through no fault of the property owner. 2. The following are exempt from the provisions of this section relating to false alarm cost recovery: a. False alarms that occur during electrical storms, earthquakes, or other severe weather conditions; b. False alarms that are activated during testing of the alarm system, provided that the fire department has been notified in advance; c. False alarms that occur within thirty (30) days after installation of a new alarm system; and d. False alarms that occur on property owned by the City of Grangeville. 3. The fire chief shall make the initial determination regarding whether an exemption applies. This determination may be appealed through the process outlined in section 6. I. Use Of Recovered Funds: All funds recovered under this chapter shall be deposited into the general fund. J. Annual Review: The city council shall review this chapter and the fee structure annually to ensure that the fees charged reflect the actual costs incurred by the city for providing fire suppression services. (Ord. 983, 7-7-2025)

laws.content:
**SECTION:**

**4-0-1: CONTRACTOR REGISTRATION NUMBER:**

No building permit will be issued without the contractor’s registration number being presented by the contractor, except when the permit applicant provides evidence to the satisfaction of the building inspector or the city clerk or their designee that the applicant is exempt from the registration requirements pursuant to title 54, chapter 52, Idaho Code. (Ord. 795, 1-23-2006)

laws.title: Building Codes
laws.content:
**SECTION:**

**4-1-1: Adoption Of Codes**

**4-1-1: ADOPTION OF CODES:**

A. Code Adoption: The approved editions of the following nationally recognized codes, as adopted by the state of Idaho or the Idaho building code board, are adopted as the official building codes of the city of Grangeville, except as provided in subsection B of this section:

1. International building code;

2. International residential code, parts I–IV and part IX;

3. International energy conservation code;

4. Uniform code for the abatement of dangerous buildings, 1997 edition; and

5. Uniform sign code, 1979 edition.

The adopted versions of the foregoing codes shall be deemed superseded by successive versions of such codes as they are adopted or approved by the Idaho building code board effective on any date such codes are made effective by the Idaho building code board.

B. Exemptions: Agricultural buildings are exempt from the building codes adopted herein, but shall remain subject to placement requirements established by Grangeville city zoning regulations. (Ord.
783, 6-6-2005)

C. Building Permit Fees:

1. Before issuing a building permit the owner, or his agent, shall pay the requisite fee to the city of Grangeville. The owner, or his agent, shall also pay any other fees charged to the city of Grangeville from other government entities for reviewing plans or permits. Fees charged are in addition to the building permit fee and are required to be paid at the time of the application. No permit shall be issued until all requisite fees are paid in full.

2. Upon failure to obtain a permit before work on a building has begun, except in emergency cases, the total fee shall be double the permit fees charged.

3. There shall be no refunds once a permit has been issued. (Ord. 874, 5-7-2012)

D. Copies On File: The city clerk shall be authorized pursuant to Idaho Code section 50-901 to maintain at least one copy of each of the codes adopted in this section in her office available to public inspection. (Ord. 783, 6-6-2005)

There is hereby adopted for the purpose of establishing minimum standards of design, materials and workmanship for all plumbing hereafter installed, altered or repaired and to establish methods of procedure with the limits of the City, that certain plumbing code known as the Idaho State Plumbing Code, being particularly the most current edition thereof, and the whole thereof, of which not less than one (1) copy has been and now is filed in the office of the City Clerk and the same is hereby adopted and incorporated as fully as though set out at length herein. (Ord. 347, 12-4-1961; amd. Ord. 956, 4-18-2022)

**CHAPTER 3**

**ELECTRICAL CODE**

4-3-1: Scope Of Code

4-3-2: Minimum Safety Standards

4-3-3: Special Requirements

4-3-4: Alterations To Existing Wiring

4-3-5: Electrical Inspector

4-3-6: Jurisdiction Of Electrical Inspector

4-3-1: SCOPE OF CODE:

The regulations of this Code shall apply to all electrical wiring and equipment installed within the corporate limits of the City, except wiring and equipment which is used for the generation, control, distribution or communication system of a utility and which is installed by or for, and owned and maintained by an electrical or communication utility operating under due authority granted by the City. Electrical wiring in Federal buildings, railway cars or automotive equipment is exempt from the requirements of this Code. (Ord. 357, 4-1-1963)

4-3-2: MINIMUM SAFETY STANDARDS:

Except as herein provided all installations of wires and equipment to convey electric current and apparatus to be operated by such current, made after the effective date of this Code, shall be in compliance with the most current Edition of the National Electrical Code, as provided by the American Standards Association, relating to such work so far as the same covers both fire and personal injury hazards, and as the National Electrical Code shall be amended, revised, compiled and published from time to time and as such amendments or revisions are adopted by the City Council. One (1) copy of the National Electrical Code as adopted shall be kept on file in the office of the City Clerk for use and examination of the public. (Ord. 671, 11-7-1994; amd. Ord. 956, 4-18-2022)

4-3-3: SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS:

All public, commercial and industrial buildings of any kind or description, including apartment buildings located within the fire zone shall be wired to conform in all respects with the National Electrical Code now in existence or as hereafter amended. (Ord. 571, 2-21-1984)

4-3-4: ALTERATIONS TO EXISTING WIRING:

When extensions and/or alterations are made to any electrical circuit in or on any buildings or structure, coming under the provisions of this Code and/or the ordinances of the City, said electrical circuit, in its entirety, shall be made to conform to such provisions of this Code as are particularly applicable thereto. (Ord. 357, 4-1-1963)

4-3-5: ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR:

The Mayor is hereby authorized and directed to enter into an agreement with the Idaho State Electrical Board, Department of Law Enforcement, to furnish electrical inspection service to the City as authorized by Idaho Code 54-1001C by a duly appointed State Electrical Inspector acting as Electrical Inspector for the City. (Ord. 357, 4-1-1963)

4-3-6: JURISDICTION OF ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR:

Except as herein provided the installation of electrical wiring or equipment in or on any building or structure within the corporate limits of the City, shall be done at all times subject to the inspection by the Electrical Inspector of the City. (Ord. 357, 4-1-1963)

4-3-7: AUTHORITY TO DISCONNECT:

If an electrical installation made after the effective date of this Code is found to be defective or defectively installed, or otherwise not in conformity with this Code the Electrical Inspector may order such installation disconnected from the source of supply until the necessary corrections have been made, provided that the owner of the premises, the tenant, if any, and the power supply company shall be notified in writing. (Ord. 357, 4-1-1963)

4-3-8: ELECTRICAL INSPECTION TAGS:

A. It shall be unlawful for any person to install or cause to be installed, any electrical wiring, or equipment coming under the provisions of this Code unless an electrical inspection tag, as authorized by Idaho Code 54-1005, or any application for such electrical inspection tag, properly completed, has been mailed to the Idaho State Electrical Board, State House, Boise, Idaho. Electrical contractors shall use the standard electrical contractors inspection tags issued to all licensed electrical contractors by the Idaho State Electrical Board. Owners installing electrical wiring or equipment on their own property shall use the standard application for owners’ electrical inspection tag which applications shall be made available at the Office of the City Clerk and at the local offices of the power suppliers.

B. The power supplier shall not connect to or energize any electrical installation coming under the provisions of this Code unless such power supplier has in possession, an electrical inspection tag, issued by the Idaho State Electrical Board, covering the installation to be authorized. (Ord. 357, 4-1-1963)

4-3-9: STATE LICENSE REQUIRED:

A. Except as herein provided it shall be unlawful for any person to perform or supervise the actual physical work of installing electric wires or equipment to convey electric current unless such person holds a valid journeyman electricians license, issued by the Idaho State Electrical Board, Department of Law Enforcement.
B. Except as herein provided it shall be unlawful for any person, partnership, company, association or corporation to engage in the business of installing electrical wires or equipment to convey electrical current or to enter into agreements to install such wires or equipment without a valid electrical contractors license issued by the Idaho State Electrical Board, Department of Law Enforcement.

Exemptions: The licensing provisions of this section shall not apply to persons making electrical installations on their own property, to apprentice electricians working under the direct, on the job, supervision of licensed journeymen electricians nor to persons regularly employed to do electrical maintenance work on their employer’s premises. (Ord. 357, 4-1-1963)

4-3-10: LIABILITY OF CITY:

This Code is not to be construed to relieve from or lesson responsibility or liability of any party owning, operating, or controlling, or installing any electrical wiring or equipment, for damages to person or property caused by any defects therein, nor shall the City be held as assuming any such liability by reason of the inspection required herein. (Ord. 357, 4-1-1963)

4-3-11: PENALTY FOR VIOLATIONS:

Any person who shall violate the provisions of this Code, or neglect or refuse to comply with any order of notice made by the electrical inspector pursuant to the provisions of this Code shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction thereof shall be subject to a fine as established in the master fee schedule. (Ord. 357, 4-1-1963; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018)

4-4-1: ADOPTION OF FIRE CODE:

There is hereby adopted, for the purpose of prescribing regulations governing conditions hazardous to life and property from fire or explosion, the most current version of the International Fire Code, as adopted by the State of Idaho, including all appendices thereto, and the same is hereby adopted and incorporated as though fully set forth at length herein.

laws.title: General Standards
laws.content:
In all areas of special flood hazards, the following standards are required:

A. Anchoring:

1. All new construction and substantial improvements shall be anchored to prevent flotation, collapse, or lateral movement of the structure resulting from hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads, including the effects of buoyancy.

2. All mobile/manufactured homes shall be anchored to resist flotation, collapse, or lateral movement by providing over-the-top and frame ties to ground anchors. Specific requirements shall be that:

   a. Over-the-top ties be provided at each of the four (4) corners of the mobile home, with two (2) additional ties per side at intermediate locations, with mobile homes less than fifty feet (50') long requiring one additional tie per side;

   b. Frame ties be provided at each corner of the home with five (5) additional ties per side at intermediate points, with mobile homes less than fifty feet (50') long requiring four (4) additional ties per side;

   c. All components of the anchoring system be capable of carrying a force of four thousand eight hundred (4,800) pounds; and

   d. Any additions to the mobile home be similarly anchored.

3. An alternative method of anchoring may involve a system designed to withstand a wind force of ninety (90) miles per hour or greater. Certification must be provided to the Building Inspector, that this standard has been met.

B. Construction Materials And Methods:

1. All new construction and substantial improvements shall be constructed with materials and utility equipment resistant to flood damage.

2. All new construction and substantial improvements shall be constructed using methods and practices that minimize flood damage.

C. Utilities:

1. All new and replacement water supply systems shall be designed to minimize or eliminate infiltration of flood waters into the system.

2. New and replacement sanitary sewage systems shall be designed to minimize or eliminate infiltration of flood waters into the systems and discharge from the systems into flood water.

3. On-site waste disposal systems shall be located to avoid impairment to them or contamination from them during flooding.

D. Development Proposals: All new development proposals, including subdivisions and manufactured home parks, shall:

1. Be consistent with the need to minimize flood damage;

2. Have public utilities and facilities such as sewer, gas, electrical, and water systems located and constructed to minimize flood damage;

3. Provide adequate drainage provided to reduce exposure to flood damage; and

4. Include base flood elevation data for all proposals greater than fifty (50) lots or five (5) acres (whichever is the lesser).

E. Review Of Building Permits: Where elevation data is not available, applications for building permits shall be reviewed to assure that proposed construction will be reasonably safe from flooding. The test of reasonableness is a local judgment and includes use of historical data, high water marks, photographs of past flooding, etc., where available. (Ord. 565, 10-3-1983; amd. Ord. 954, 12-20-2021)

laws.title: Specific Standards
laws.content:
In all areas of special flood hazards where base flood elevation data has been provided as set forth in Section 4-5-3-2, Basis for Establishing the Areas of Special Flood Hazard, or Subsection 4-5-4-3B, Use of Other Base Flood Data, the following provisions are required:

A. Residential Construction: New construction and substantial improvement of any residential structure shall have the lowest floor, including basement, elevated to or above base flood elevation.

B. Nonresidential Construction: New construction and substantial improvement of any commercial, industrial or other nonresidential structure shall either have the lowest floor, including basement, elevated to the level of the base flood elevation; or, together with attendant utility and sanitary facilities, shall:

1. Be floodproofed so that below the base flood level the structure is watertight with walls substantially impermeable to the passage of water.

2. Have structural components capable of resisting hydrostatic and hydrodynamic loads and effects of buoyancy.

3. Be certified by a registered professional engineer or architect that the standards of this subsection are satisfied. Such certifications shall be provided to the official as set forth in Subsection 4-5-4-3C2.

C. Manufactured Homes:

1. Manufactured homes shall be anchored in accordance with Subsection 4-5-5-1A.

2. For manufactured homes outside of a manufactured home park or subdivision; new manufactured home parks or subdivisions; for expansions to existing manufactured home parks or subdivisions; existing manufactured home park or subdivision where a manufactured home has incurred “substantial damage” as a result of a flood; require that:

   a. Manufactured homes are elevated on a permanent foundation so that the lowest floor of the manufactured home will be at or above the base flood elevation; and be securely anchored to an adequately anchored foundation system to resist flotation collapse and lateral movement;

   b. Adequate surface drainage and access for a hauler are provided; and

   c. In the instance of elevation on pilings, that:

      (1) Lots are large enough to permit steps;

      (2) Piling foundations are placed in stable soil no more than ten feet (10') apart; and

      (3) Reinforcement is provided for pilings more than six feet (6') above the ground level.

D. Standards For Recreational Vehicles: All recreational vehicles placed on site shall:
1. Be on site for fewer than one hundred eighty (180) consecutive days;

2. Be fully licensed and ready for highway use. A recreational vehicle is ready for highway use if it is on its wheels or jacking system, is attached to the site only by quick disconnect type utilities and security devices, and has no permanently attached additions; or

3. Meet the permit requirements of Section 4-5-4 of this Chapter and the applicable elevation and anchoring requirements for manufactured homes in Subsection 4-5-5-2C.

E. Construction Of Below-Grade Crawlspace:

1. The interior grade of a crawlspace must not be below the BFE and must not be more than two feet (2') below the exterior lowest adjacent grade (LAG).

2. The height of the below-grade crawlspace, measured from the interior grade of the crawlspace to the top of the crawlspace foundation wall, must not exceed four feet (4') at any point.

3. There must be an adequate drainage system that removes floodwaters from the interior area of the crawlspace. The enclosed area should be drained within a reasonable time after a flood event.

4. The velocity of floodwaters at the site should not exceed five feet (5') per second for any crawlspace.

5. See Technical Bulletin 11 for further information.

6. Caution: Buildings that have below-grade crawlspace will have higher flood insurance premiums than buildings that have the preferred crawlspace construction, with the interior elevation of the crawlspace soil at or above the Base Flood Elevation (BFE). (Ord. 565, 10-3-1983; amd. Ord. 954, 12-20-2021)

4-5-5-3: FLOODWAYS:

Located within areas of special flood hazard established in Section 4-5-3-2 are areas designed as floodways. Since the floodway is an extremely hazardous area due to the velocity of flood waters which carry debris, potential projectiles, and erosion potential, the following provisions apply:

A. Prohibit encroachments, including fill, new construction, substantial improvements, and other development within the adopted regulatory floodway unless it has been demonstrated through hydrologic and hydraulic analyses performed in accordance with standard engineering practice that the proposed encroachment shall not result in any increase in flood levels during the occurrence of the base flood discharge.

B. If Subsection A is satisfied, all new construction and substantial improvements shall comply with all applicable flood hazard reduction provisions of Section 4-5-5, Provisions for Flood Hazard Reduction. (Ord. 565, 10-3-1983; amd. Ord. 954, 12-20-2021)
