No person licensed under this chapter or any employee of licensee shall impersonate or hold himself out to be a peace officer of this State, nor shall he operate or permit to be operated a motor vehicle with a siren, blinker light, or any insignia thereon bearing a likeness to the insignia used by peace officers of this State.

B. No insignia used by any private security officer shall include the word police at any place within the insignia. (Ord. 579, 4-1-1985)

5-7-17: REQUIREMENTS FOR EMPLOYEES:

A. All persons to be hired by licensee as private security officers for a period of time not to exceed five (5) days shall have provided to the Chief of Police their fingerprints, photograph, and proper identification, for the purpose of NCIC investigation, and will not be permitted the carrying or use of firearms.

B. All persons to be hired by licensee as private security officers for a period of time in excess of five (5) days shall complete an application similar to that required in section 5-7-3 of this chapter along with fingerprints and photograph, which will be recorded with the Chief of Police. The Chief of Police may, at his discretion, cause an investigation to be opened, and may make recommendations to the licensee as to the character and favorability of the applicant. Provided the applicant meets the standards as set forth in subsection C1 of this Section, the acceptability of applicant lies at the discretion of the licensee.

C. Standards to be met by applicants:

1. All applicants will be citizens of the United States.

2. All applicants will be in possession of a valid Idaho driver’s license.

3. Applicant has not been convicted of a driving while intoxicated offense or vehicular homicide offense within the year preceding application.

4. Applicant has not been convicted of any felony of this State or any other state in the ten (10) years previous to this date of application and is not on parole or probation for any reason at the time of the application. Additionally, if the application or the subsequent investigation reflects any felony record of the applicant, then additionally the applicant shall have lived within Idaho County, Idaho, for a one year period immediately preceding the date of the application.

5. Applicant must be of good moral character.

D. The applicant will be issued by licensee, upon hiring, a certificate stating his name, address, age, social security number, position of employment, address of employer, his status regarding firearms possession, and whether his employment is of a temporary (5 days or less) or a permanent nature. (Ord. 579, 4-1-1985)

5-7-18: SAVE HARMLESS AGREEMENT:

A save harmless agreement will be filed with the City upon the approval of license, in order to release the City from responsibility for the actions of the licensee or any of his employees. (Ord. 579, 4-1-1985)

laws.title: Trailer Courts and Trailer Coaches
laws.content:
**SECTION:**

5-9-1: Definitions

5-9-2: Application; Trailer Court

5-9-3: Trailer Court License

5-9-4: Register

5-9-5: Domestic Animals

5-9-6: License Transfer

5-9-7: Application; Trailer Coach

5-9-8: Trailer Coach License Fee

5-9-9: Location Of Trailer Coaches

5-9-10: Permit Renewal; Trailer Coach

5-9-11: Location Restrictions

5-9-12: Revocation

5-9-13: Posting Of License

**5-9-1: DEFINITIONS:**

DEPENDENT TRAILER COACH: One which does not have a water closet and bathtub or shower.

INDEPENDENT TRAILER COACH: One that has a water closet and a bathtub or shower.

SERVICE BUILDING: A building housing communal toilet, laundry and other sanitary facilities necessary for the health and convenience of the trailer occupants.

TRAILER COACH: A vehicle without means of self-propulsion, but licensable as a conveyance on public streets or highways, and which is constructed to permit occupancy as a dwelling or sleeping place for one or more persons.

TRAILER COACH SPACE: A plot of ground within a trailer court designated for the accommodation of one trailer coach.

TRAILER COURT: Any plot of ground upon which two (2) or more occupied trailer coaches are located. (1959 Code)

**5-9-2: APPLICATION; TRAILER COURT:**

Applications for a trailer court license shall be filed with and issued by the City Clerk. Application shall be in writing signed by the applicant and shall contain the following:

A. The name and address of the applicant.

B. The location and legal description of the trailer court.

C. Such further information as may be requested by the Governing Body to enable it to determine if the proposed location will comply with legal requirements, including a sketch or plot plan designating numbered trailer spaces.

No change or alteration in the plot plan shall be made without first making a written application for such change or alteration to the Governing Body and receiving a written permit therefrom.

The Governing Body shall investigate the location and if it is found to be in compliance with all provisions of this chapter and all other applicable chapters or statutes, application may be approved. (1959 Code)

**5-9-3: TRAILER COURT LICENSE:**

Any person who maintains or operates a trailer court must first obtain a license from the City Clerk which license must be approved by the Governing Body of the City. The fee for such trailer court shall be as established in the master fee schedule. (1959 Code; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018)

**5-9-4: REGISTER:**

It shall be the duty of the licensee to keep a register containing a record of all trailer coaches occupying space within the court. The register shall contain the following information:

A. Name and address of each occupant in each trailer coach.

B. Make, model and year of all automobiles and trailer coaches.

C. License numbers and owner of each trailer coach and automobile by which it is towed.

D. The state issuing such licenses.

E. The date of arrival and departure of each trailer coach and the number or other identification of the space or spaces occupied. The court shall keep the register available for inspection at all times by law enforcement officers, public health officials and other officials whose duties necessitate acquisition of the information contained in the register. The register records shall not be destroyed until after a period of three (3) years following the date of registration. (1959 Code)

**5-9-5: DOMESTIC ANIMALS:**

No domestic animals or house pets shall be allowed to run at large or commit any nuisances within the limits of a trailer court. (1959 Code)

**5-9-6: LICENSE TRANSFER:**

All licenses issued hereunder for a trailer court and trailer coach shall be personal to the licensee and be nontransferable without the written consent of the governing body first being obtained. (1959 Code)

**5-9-7: APPLICATION; TRAILER COACH:**

Application for a trailer coach license shall be filed with and issued by the City Clerk. Application shall be in writing signed by the applicant and shall contain the following:

A. The name and address of the applicant.

B. The location and description where trailer coach is to be parked.

C. Such further information as may be requested by the governing body. (1959 Code)

**5-9-8: TRAILER COACH LICENSE FEE:**

There shall be imposed by the City retroactive to the date of January 1, 1965, no trailer coach fee charged to each applicant for licenses required hereunder. However, a license and application therefor must be made in accordance with the terms of this Chapter. All licenses so issued shall expire on December 31 of each year. (Ord. 372, 1-11-1965)

**5-9-9: LOCATION OF TRAILER COACHES:**

The use of trailer coaches as trailer or otherwise, occupied by one or more persons, except in an approved public or private trailer court, shall be considered as a public nuisance unless the yards surrounding it comply with the requirements for a dwelling as established by the zoning provisions of this Code. (Ord. 328, 8-10-1959)

Notes
1. See Title 10 of this Code.

**5-9-10: PERMIT RENEWAL; TRAILER COACH:**

It shall be unlawful for any person to occupy a trailer coach or for any person who is the owner, renter or lessee of any property within the City to erect or give consent for the placement and occupancy of any trailer house within the City except in an approved public trailer court or in an approved trailer coach space.

It shall be unlawful to park a trailer coach, whether occupied or not, on any public thoroughfare or public place, other than in an approved trailer court for more than four (4) hours.

Trailer coaches may be parked on private property and occupied by a person or persons for a period of time specified in the permit issued under Section 5-9-8 of this Chapter. A permit for such use and occupancy must be obtained in compliance with Section 5-9-8, within forty eight (48) hours after the trailer is parked. (Ord. 328, 8-10-1959)

**5-9-11: LOCATION RESTRICTIONS:**

Placement and use of trailer coaches occupied by any person on other than approved public or private courts must be so arranged as not to interfere with the rights and privileges of adjacent property owners, each occupied trailer coach being considered as a separate dwelling house under the laws of the zoning ordinance 1. (1959 Code)

Notes

1. See Title 10 of this Code.

**5-9-12: REVOCATION:**

The governing body may revoke or suspend any license issued in this Chapter when such licensee shall have been found guilty of a violation of this Chapter or any part of this Code. (1959 Code)

**5-9-13: POSTING OF LICENSE:**

A license issued under this Chapter shall be conspicuously posted on the individual trailer coach not located within a trailer court or in the office of or on the premises of the trailer court. (1959 Code)

laws.title: Hotels and Motels
laws.content:
**SECTION:**

5-10-1: Hotel Regulations

5-10-2: Motel Regulations

**5-10-1: HOTEL REGULATIONS:**

A. Definition: Every building maintained or advertised as a public lodging house or where more than six (6) rooms are provided for sleeping accommodations shall be known as a hotel.

B. Fire Protection Equipment: The Fire Chief, or other officer designated by the governing body, shall survey each hotel and specify suitable fire detecting devices or extinguishing appliances which shall be provided.

Such devices or appliances may consist of automatic sprinkler or water spray systems, standpipe and hose, fixed or portable fire extinguishers or other suitable fire extinguishing systems.

C. Maintenance Of Equipment: Fire protective or extinguishing systems or appliances which have been installed in compliance with any permit or order, or according to any provisions of this Code, shall be maintained in operative condition at all times and it shall be unlawful for any owner or occupant to reduce the effectiveness of the protection so required.

D. Inspection: It shall be the duty of the Fire Chief and the Health Officer, or other officers so designated by the governing body, to make periodic and regular inspections of every hotel and to make regular reports to the governing body of such hotel or hotels concerning regulations imposed by this Code.

E. Hotel Register: A register shall be maintained at every hotel and each guest shall be required to register his name and home address. The date of arrival and departure shall be clearly indicated and the register shall be maintained for a period of at least one year following registration. The register shall be open for inspection to any authorized person. (1959 Code)

**5-10-2: MOTEL REGULATIONS:**

A. Building Permit Required: Before construction of a motel is started, an application for a permit for such construction shall be submitted to the City Clerk. The City Clerk shall present such application to the governing body for its approval. Only after approval of the governing body shall a permit for construction of a motel be issued.

B. Service Station Restrictions: Automobile service stations shall be located no closer than fifty feet (50') to any motel.

C. Parking Space On Premises: Each unit of a motel or tourist court shall be provided with an assigned parking space entirely on the premises.

D. Minimum Requirements: The minimum space for each unit shall be twelve feet by twenty feet (12' x 20') and shall contain one full bath, toilet facilities, dressing compartment and sleeping room.

E. Existing Standards: The plumbing, heating and ventilation components shall meet all local fire, plumbing and building code requirements.

F. Application To Include Plan: Each application for a motel or tourist court shall be submitted with a complete plan, including the plot plan and adjacent buildings, parking arrangement and driveways, unit sizes, plumbing and heating layout, accessory uses, materials to be used, front and rear elevations and architectural design.

G. Guests Required To Register: Every operator of a motel shall maintain a register in which each guest shall register his name, home address and license number of the vehicle in which he is traveling. The date of his arrival and departure shall also be recorded. Such register shall be available to any authorized person inspecting the motel and shall be preserved for a period of not less than one year. (1959 Code)

laws.title: General Offenses
laws.content:
**SECTION:** 6-1-1: Effect Of Regulations 6-1-2: Barbed Wire And Electric Fences 6-1-3: Cruelty To Animals 6-1-4: Deposit Of Injurious Material On Thoroughfares 6-1-5: Disorderly Conduct 6-1-6: Expectorating (Spitting) On Sidewalks Or In Public Buildings 6-1-7: Offense, General 6-1-8: Indecent Exposure 6-1-9: Keeping Of Junk Restricted 6-1-10: Loudspeakers Or Sound Trucks 6-1-11: Lug Wheels Prohibited 6-1-12: Mufflers; Unnecessary Noise 6-1-13: Obscene Conduct 6-1-14: Water Flowing Upon Streets 6-1-15: Windowsills To Be Kept Clear 6-1-16: Abandoned Iceboxes, Refrigerators Or Containers 6-1-17: Weapons Prohibited 6-1-18: Trapping Regulations 6-1-1: EFFECT OF REGULATIONS: A. It shall be unlawful for any person to do any act forbidden or fail to perform any act required herein. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002) B. Any violation of this chapter shall constitute a misdemeanor and be punishable by imprisonment in the County Jail not exceeding six (6) months, or by a fine as established in the master fee schedule, or by both. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018) 6-1-2: BARBED WIRE AND ELECTRIC FENCES: It shall be unlawful for any person to erect or maintain any electric fence or other fence constructed in whole or in part of barbed wire or to use barbed wire as a guard to any parking lot or parcel of land. A. Barbed Wire Fences: 1. Barbed wire fences shall be allowed within the incorporated limits of the City in the following places only: a. In any zone which permits the maintenance of livestock. b. As a guard atop a fence of at least six feet (6') high for security purposes within the industrial or commercial zone of the City. B. Electric Fences: Electric fences shall not be permitted at any place within the incorporated limits of the City. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002) 6-1-3: CRUELTY TO ANIMALS: It shall be unlawful for any person to torture or beat cruelly, starve or otherwise ill treat any animal in his care or charge, whether belonging to themselves or any other person. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002) 6-1-4: DEPOSITS OF INJURIOUS MATERIAL ON THOROUGHFARES: It shall be unlawful for any person to deposit, place or allow to remain in or upon any public thoroughfare any material or substance injurious to person or property. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002) 6-1-5: DISORDERLY CONDUCT: Every person is guilty of disorderly conduct when that person willfully engages in violent, tumultuous or offensive conduct; or by threatening, quarrelling, or challenging to fight another person; or fights with another person in a public place; or makes noise that is unreasonable, considering the nature of the actor’s conduct, location, time of day or night, and other factors that would govern the conduct of a reasonably prudent person under the circumstances; or engages in violent, noisy or riotous behavior that would be frightening or offensive to a reasonable person who might be expected to be in the vicinity. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002; amd. Ord. 955, 3-21-2022) 6-1-6: EXPECTORATING (SPITTING) ON SIDEWALKS OR IN PUBLIC BUILDINGS: It shall be unlawful for any person to expectorate or spit upon any sidewalk, public way or upon the floor of any public building or room used for public assemblies. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002) 6-1-7: OFFENSE, GENERAL: It shall be unlawful for any person to commit any act or fail to perform any requirement which is prohibited or required by state law or city code, insofar as such laws are applicable to municipal government. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002) 6-1-8: INDECENT EXPOSURE: It shall be unlawful for any person to appear in a state of nudity or in any indecent or lewd dress or condition in any public place or in any such place to make any indecent exposure of his/her person or private parts thereof or the private parts of another or to conduct themselves in a lewd or lascivious manner. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002) 6-1-9: KEEPING OF JUNK RESTRICTED: It shall be unlawful for any person to store or keep any old articles or materials which may be classified as junk, adjacent to or in close proximity to any school, house, church, public park, public grounds, business buildings, or residences without first providing proper and tight buildings for the storage of same. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002) 6-1-10: LOUDSPEAKERS OR SOUND TRUCKS: It shall be unlawful to play, operate or use any device known as a sound truck, loudspeaker or sound amplifier, radio or phonograph, with loudspeaker or sound amplifier or any instrument of any kind or character which emits loud and raucous noise and is attached to and upon any vehicle unless such person in charge of such vehicle shall have first applied to and received a permit from the city of Grangeville to operate any such vehicle so equipped. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002) 6-1-11: LUG WHEELS PROHIBITED: It shall be unlawful for tractors, or other vehicles with wheels injurious to pavement to be permitted upon the public thoroughfares unless the operator of such vehicle shall first plank such streets or place rubber treads on wheels. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002) 6-1-12: MUFFLERS; UNNECESSARY NOISE: It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a motor vehicle which shall, at all times, be equipped with a muffler upon the exhaust thereof in good working order and in constant operation to prevent excessive or unusual noise and it shall be unlawful for any person operating any motor vehicle to use a cutout, bypass or similar muffler elimination appliance. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002) 6-1-13: OBSCENE CONDUCT: It shall be unlawful for any person to urinate or stool in any place open to the public view, or to be guilty of any lewd, lascivious or obscene conduct or to sing any lewd or obscene song, ballad or other words in any public place or any other place where other persons are present or to indecently, exhibit any animal. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002) 6-1-14: WATER FLOWING UPON STREETS: It shall be unlawful for any person to allow any water to flow into or upon any public thoroughfare. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002) 6-1-15: WINDOWSILLS TO BE KEPT CLEAR: It shall be unlawful for any person to place or keep on any windowsill, porch or other projection above the first story of any building abutting on any sidewalk any article which might do injury by falling upon any person on the sidewalk in front of such building, unless said article be securely fastened or protected by screens. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002) 6-1-16: ABANDONED ICEBOXES, REFRIGERATORS OR CONTAINERS: It shall be unlawful for any person to leave or permit to remain outside of any dwelling, building or other structure, or within any unoccupied or abandoned building, dwelling or other structure under their control, in a place accessible to children, any abandoned, unattended or discarded icebox, refrigerator or other container which has a door or lid, snaplock, or other locking device which may not be released from the inside, without first removing said door or lid, snaplock or other locking device, or by first fastening, bolting or locking the same in such a manner that it is impossible to open the same by the use of the hands. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002) 6-1-17: WEAPONS PROHIBITED: A. Definition: Whenever the term “weapon” is used in this section, the term shall mean any instrument, used in the propulsion of shot, shell or bullets or other harmful objects by the action of gunpowder exploded within it, or by the action of compressed air within it, or by the power of springs, rubber bands, or by the power of a bow and string, and including what are commonly known as air rifles and BB guns, slingshots, bow and arrows, etc. B. Concealed Weapons: Without a properly issued concealed weapons permit, it shall be unlawful for any person to carry concealed upon his person any brass knuckles, revolver, pistol, dagger, stiletto or other deadly weapon. C. Discharge Of Weapons Prohibited: It shall be unlawful for any person to discharge weapons of any kind or description within the limits of the city; provided however, that this shall not apply to police officers in the discharge of their duties. D. Exceptions; Permits: The city council may at any time, upon receipt of proper application, grant permits to shooting galleries, gun clubs and others for shooting in fixed localities and under specified rules. Such permits shall be in writing attested by the city clerk conforming to such requirements as the city council shall demand, and the permit thus issued shall be subject to revocation at any time by action of the governing body. (Ord. 753, 10-21-2002) 6-1-18: TRAPPING REGULATIONS: A. Definitions: TRAP: Any mechanical device or snare which is designed to hold, capture, and/or kill an animal including, but not limited to, live traps, steel jaw foothold traps, padded jaw traps, body gripping (Conitbear) traps, snares, deadfalls, leg hold type traps, or similar devices. B. Setting Traps Prohibited; Exceptions: Unless authorized by the Idaho department of fish and game, pursuant to Idaho Code title 36, chapter 11, no person shall set a trap to catch an animal (other than a mouse, rat, gopher, vole, or mole) within the city limits, except a person specifically authorized by the council or by the chief of police or designee. C. Penalties: Any person violating these provisions shall be deemed guilty of an infraction and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished pursuant to this code and the Idaho Code, unless otherwise specifically provided for. (Ord. 881, 12-17-2012) **CHAPTER 2** **ANIMAL CONTROL** SECTION: 6-2-1: Purpose 6-2-2: Definitions 6-2-3: Violations 6-2-4: Fees For Licensing, Impounding And Boarding 6-2-5: Procedures 6-2-6: Duties Of Animal Control Officer 6-2-7: Impoundment Of Dogs And Other Animals 6-2-8: Violations And Remedies Cumulative 6-2-9: Penalty For Violation 6-2-1: PURPOSE: The city is concerned about the welfare of dogs and other animals, owned, harbored and possessed within the city limits and about the responsibility of the owners, harborers and other persons possessing such animals. This chapter provides for the licensing of dogs and for the disposition of dogs found without such license having been paid; prohibiting imitation license tags; providing for the examination for rabies and the disposition of rabid dogs; providing for impounding of dogs, and fees therefor; providing for the prohibition of any dog or other animals, running at large; providing a penalty, for keeping or harboring any dog without paying a license therefor or permitting any dog to run at large; prohibit the harboring of a barking dog; prohibiting dogs and other animals in city parks; prohibiting the running at large of female dogs in heat; prohibiting a vicious dog to run at large; prohibiting a sick dog to run at large; prohibiting the owning of, harboring of or possession of exotic animals; providing a penalty thereof; providing for the duties of the chief of police and his designated assistant; declaring interference with any officer to be unlawful. (Ord. 699, 2-18-1997; amd. Ord. 939, 11-18-2019) 6-2-2: DEFINITIONS:
ANIMAL: Any domestic animal that has been tamed and kept by humans as a work animal, food source, or pet. Domestic cats are excluded from this chapter, unless specifically included herein.
ANIMAL CONTROL OFFICER: The chief of police; all police officers of the city; and any other person designated by the city as animal control officer.
AT LARGE; DOGS/ANIMALS: Whenever any dog or other animal shall be found upon any of the streets or alleys of the city, or on the premises of any persons, firm or corporation who are not the owner of said animal, and not being actually led or driven by some person in charge, they shall be deemed at large.
CAT: A small carnivorous mammal long domesticated and kept by man as a pet for catching rats and mice. This does not include any other members of the cat family.
DANGEROUS DOG: Any dog declared dangerous as provided in this chapter.
DOG: Any member, male or female, of the family of Canis familiaris.
EXOTIC ANIMAL/WILD ANIMALS: Any animal which is considered a wild animal or is inherently dangerous.
HARBOR/HARBORIN G: To own or keep a dog within the city limits. It shall be prima facie evidence that a person is harboring a dog if the person is listed as the owner of the dog on any application for dog licensing; or is over eighteen (18) years of age and resides at or is in physical control of a premises, or part thereof, on which a dog remains or to which it customarily returns daily for food or water.
HARBORER/OWNER: Any person harboring or keeping a dog within the corporate limits of the city.
KENNEL: Any premises, other than a veterinary office, on which four (4) or more dogs are maintained, harbored, possessed, boarded, bred or cared for, trained, or sold, which are over four (4) months of age.
LEASH: A leash, lead, cord, or chain not more than ten feet (10') in length, by which an animal is physically controlled by the person accompanying it.
NEUTERED/SPAYED DOG: Any dog rendered incapable of producing offspring by surgery or other veterinary medical procedure.
PREMISES: All real property under a harborer’s ownership, lease or control inside the inner line of a sidewalk, or if no sidewalk, inside the curb, ditch or shoulder marking the edge of the traveled or used portion of the public right of way. Premises also includes the inside of a closed motor vehicle.
RABIES VACCINATION: A vaccination given by a licensed veterinarian, to a dog for the prevention of rabies, and a certificate of vaccination is issued, with a certification that the vaccination is valid for a specified period of time as designated by the veterinarian.
UNDER CONTROL: A dog is under control if:
A. The dog is confined within the boundaries of the harborer’s premises; or
B. The dog is not on the harborer’s premises but is confined within a vehicle or in the control of a responsible person by use of a leash not exceeding ten feet (10') in length; or
C. The dog is secure in the bed of a vehicle in such a manner that, the animal cannot reach the side rails of the vehicle bed.
(Ord. 699, 2-18-1997; amd. Ord. 745, 1-7-2002; Ord. 939, 11-18-2019)
6-2-3: VIOLATIONS: A. Dogs/Animals Running At Large Prohibited: All owners/harborers responsible for dogs/animals kept within the city limits shall keep such animals under control or confined at all times. It shall be unlawful to allow dogs/animals to run at large. Violations of this subsection shall be an infraction and shall be punishable as provided in Idaho Code section 18-113(A). B. Poultry Running At Large Prohibited: It shall be unlawful to allow fowl or poultry to run at large. Violation shall be a misdemeanor. C. Keeping Of Stallions, Jacks, Bulls and Hogs: It shall be unlawful to keep a stallion, jack, bull or hog within the city limits. Violation shall be a misdemeanor. D. Permitting Horses On Sidewalks: It shall be unlawful for any person to allow or permit any horse, owned by him or in his custody or control, to go upon, be ridden upon or be led upon any sidewalk in the city. Violation shall be a misdemeanor. E. Shod Horses On Paved Streets: It shall be unlawful for any person to permit any shod horse, owned by or in their control, to go upon, be ridden upon or be led upon any paved street in the city, when such street has been closed to such traffic, and posted, by order of the chief of police or street superintendent when it appears that such traffic would damage the surface of said streets. Violation shall be a misdemeanor. F. License Required: It shall be unlawful for any owner/harborer to own, keep or possess a dog within the city without procuring a license as provided by this chapter. Violation shall be a misdemeanor. Any person visiting the city for not longer than thirty (30) days, and having a dog licensed from another city shall be exempt. G. Collar And Tag: Every dog shall at all times wear a substantial durable collar to which shall be securely attached the required license. Violation shall be a misdemeanor. H. Imitation License Tags Prohibited: It shall be unlawful for any owner/harborer to allow any dog kept or possessed within the city to wear any license tag or indicia of licensing other than a valid license tag issued under this chapter for the dog wearing this tag. Violation shall be a misdemeanor. This section shall not prohibit the wearing of nonlicense tags for the purpose of identification or rabies. I. Female Dogs in Heat: It shall be unlawful for any owner/harborer to allow any female dog in heat, outside of a controlled area when in heat. Violation shall be a misdemeanor. Any dog at large, in heat, may be disposed of by the animal control officer without giving any notice. J. Vicious Dogs Within The City Prohibited: It shall be unlawful for any owner/harborer to maintain a vicious dog within the city limits. Violation shall be a misdemeanor. K. Vicious Or Sick Dog At Large Prohibited: It shall be unlawful for any owner/harborer to allow a vicious or sick dog to run at large. Violation shall be a misdemeanor. L. Dogs and Other Animals Prohibited in City Parks: With the exception from the creek to the east end of Grangeville Lions Club Park as designated, it shall be unlawful for any owner/harborer to allow any dog or other animal to be within or upon those areas known as city parks: i.e., Pioneer park, Grangeville Lions Club park, Jaycee park. Violation shall be a misdemeanor. It shall be unlawful for any owner/harborer to allow any dog, or other animal to deposit feces within or upon City parks. Violation shall be an infraction, punishable by a fine as established in the master fee schedule. M. Barking Dogs: No person shall own, harbor or otherwise be responsible for any dog within the City that shall bark or growl, so as to unreasonably disturb the peace or quiet of any other person. Violation shall be a misdemeanor. N. Exotic Animals: It shall be unlawful for any owner/harborer to own, possess, or harbor any exotic animal within the City limits without application to and approval by the City Council. Violation shall be a misdemeanor. O. Kennels: It shall be unlawful for any owner/harborer to maintain a kennel within the City limits, with the exception of those kennels that are allowed in accordance with the zoning title. Violation shall be a misdemeanor. P. Nonvaccinated Dog: It shall be unlawful for any owner/harborer to own, possess, or harbor a dog within the city limits that does not have a valid rabies vaccination. Violation shall be a misdemeanor. Q. Interference Prohibited: It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly hinder, molest or interfere with any animal control officer in the discharge of any of their duties. In addition, it shall be unlawful for any person to attempt to remove and/or remove any dog or dogs from the city pound or the possession of the animal control officer, without the consent of the animal control officer or otherwise as provided by this chapter. Violation shall be a misdemeanor. R. General Offense: It shall be unlawful for any owner/harborer to: 1. Allow any dog or animal under their control to scatter garbage, refuse or debris. 2. Allow any dog or animal under their control to chase any person, vehicle or other animal. 3. Allow any dog or animal under their control to deposit fecal material on any property not that of its owner/harborer without immediately removing same from the property. 4. Harbor one or more dogs, cats, or animals in such a manner that the keeping of the dogs, cats, or animals results in a nauseous, foul or offensive odor or so as to create a public nuisance. 5. Harbor a dog, cat, or animal and fail to provide the dog, cat, or animal with food, water, shelter, or necessary veterinary care. Violation shall be a misdemeanor. (Ord. 699, 2-18-1997; amd. Ord. 746, 1-7-2002, Ord. 896, 3-2-2015; Ord. 925, 10-1-2018; Ord. 939, 11-18-2019) **Notes** 1. See title 10 of this Code. **6-2-4: FEES FOR LICENSING, IMPOUNDING AND BOARDING:** All fees shall be as established in the master fee schedule. All owners/harborers, prior to having license issued, must display to the licensing authority a current rabies vaccination. To receive the spayed or neutered rate, a valid certification from a licensed veterinarian, showing the dog has been neutered or spayed, must be displayed to the licensing authority. (Res. 136, 2-18-1997; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018; Ord. 939, 11-18-2019) **6-2-5: PROCEDURES:** A. Violations: All owners/harborers shall receive from the animal control officer one written warning for violations of subsections 6-2-3A through P of this chapter with the exceptions of subsections 6-2-3J, J, K and P of this chapter. All owners/harborers that have received a written warning and not corrected the violation shall be issued a uniform citation. The animal control officer, shall be authorized to issue a citation to any person whom the officer has probable cause to believe has violated any of the provision of this Chapter. The citation shall be issued upon a form that is approved for use for the prosecution of general misdemeanors by the Magistrate’s Division of the Third Court for the Second Judicial District, for the State of Idaho, at Grangeville. The citation shall be prepared in accordance with the existing statutes of the State of Idaho for processing general misdemeanors as from time to time shall be prescribed by the Idaho State Legislature. 1. A violation of subsection 6-2-3J, Female Dogs In Heat, will immediately be impounded, any animal in heat may be disposed of by the animal control officer without giving any notice. 2. A violation of subsection 6-2-3K, Vicious Or Sick Dog At Large, the animal control officer, may immediately and without giving notice, dispose of by destroying in a humane manner any dog found running at large which in the judgment of the officer: a. Displays symptoms of contagious disease; or b. Displays serious physical injury or illness such that the officer deems, in the officer’s sole discretion, that it is necessary to destroy the animal to prevent further suffering; or c. Displays vicious or aggressive behavior which poses an imminent risk of physical injury to any person and the dog cannot, in the discretion of the animal control officer, be taken into control for impoundment by reasonable humane methods. 3. A violation of subsection 6-2-3J, Vicious Dogs Within The City, the animal control officer, may declare a dog to be a dangerous dog if, upon investigation of any complaint, incident or information otherwise provided, the officer finds that: a. The dog has, whether or not under control, aggressively bitten any person, domestic animal or fowl or maliciously damaged or destroyed personal property of another; b. The dog has been declared dangerous, vicious or other similar declaration by any governmental authority. If the officer makes said declaration, the officer shall notify the owner/harborer of the declaration and the manner and time limits in which an appeal of the declaration may be taken. In addition, a uniform citation shall be issued to the owner/harborer for violation of subsection 6-2-3J. Said notice shall be in writing and served by, personal service, or regular first class U.S. mail addressed to the last known mailing address of the owner/harborer, with service being effective on the date of mailing. 4. The officer may impound the dog declared to be dangerous, including but not limited to impounding of the dog during the pendency of any appeal proceeding. The owner/harborer of the dog shall be liable for all costs and fees of impoundment regardless of the final disposition of the case. The owner/harborer of a dog declared dangerous shall have five (5) business days from the date of service of the written declaration to request a hearing appealing the declaration. The request shall be in writing, identifying the name, address and telephone number of the requesting party, and shall be served upon the City Clerk within the time and in the manner above provided. In the event no hearing is requested within the time and in the manner above provided the officer may dispose of the dog in a humane manner, without further notice to the owner/harborer. If a hearing is requested, a hearing shall be held within fifteen (15) days of the date, the request for hearing is received by the City Clerk, or at such other times as set by the City Council and the requesting party. a. The City Council shall constitute the hearing panel and shall hear the appeal. The hearing shall be informal and the Idaho Rules of Evidence shall not apply. The owner/harborer and the animal control officer, or other representative of the City shall be given the opportunity to submit evidence, present witnesses and be heard on the matter, including the right of cross-examination. b. In determining whether the dog is dangerous, the hearing panel may consider among other evidence, past incidents, provocation for the dangerous behavior, and the premises where the dog was harbored, the legal status of the alleged victim on the premises and any other fact or allegation relating to the incident from which the declaration arises. If the hearing panel shall find that the declaration was proper, the hearing panel shall either: a. Direct the animal control officer to dispose of the dog as directed by this Chapter. b. Direct that the dog may be released to the owner/harborer on such conditions as the hearing panel shall deem in the best interest of the City, which may include, but are not limited to, that: (1) The dog will be removed from the City limits immediately following release and not allowed to return. (2) Require the owner/harborer to take steps sufficient to confine the dog in a manner to prevent harm to the public. (3) Require the owner/harborer to provide a surety bond or proof of liability insurance for compensation of those who may suffer injury by reason of harboring of a dangerous dog. The decision of the hearing panel shall become final, unless the decision is appealed to the District Court within three (3) days, following the date of the decision. 5. A violation of subsection 6-2-3P, Non-Vaccinated Dog shall result in the immediate issuance of a uniform citation to the owner/harborer of the animal, with written instructions to have the dog vaccinated within three (3) days. B. Licenses; Application And Fees: All dog licenses shall be issued for the calendar year January 1 through December 31 of each and every year. The owner/harborer shall make application to the animal control officer, or the City clerk’s office, and pay a license fee as established in the master fee schedule, for each dog maintained within the City limits. 1. Upon receipt of the application and payment of the fees, and upon issuance of a receipt, stating the owner’s/harborer’s name, sex of the dog, breed, color, age, address, phone number, any markings of the animal, and whether the animal is neutered/spayed, a metal license shall be issued bearing the number corresponding to that upon the receipt. 2. Upon satisfactory proof that a license has been lost, a new tag of a different number may be issued upon payment of a fee as established in the master fee schedule. 3. The owner/harborer shall when applying for an animal license display to the animal control officer, or City Clerk’s office, a valid certificate of rabies vaccination, issued by a veterinarian, which shows that the dog has a current vaccination, during the period the license is issued for. All rabies vaccinations must be given as frequently as deemed necessary by a licensed veterinarian. 4. The owner/harborer shall when applying for a neutered/spayed reduction of cost for a license, must show to the animal control officer, or City Clerk’s office, a valid certification issued by a licensed veterinarian, that the animal being license, has been spayed or neutered. If a certification is not shown, the full license fee must be paid. (Ord. 699, 2-18-1997; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018; Ord. 939, 11-18-2019) **6-2-6: DUTIES OF ANIMAL CONTROL OFFICER:** The Chief of Police and all police officers of the City are designated as animal control officers. In addition to all authority granted to them for general enforcement of laws as peace officers, said officers are further authorized and directed to enforce all provisions of this chapter and perform all duties of animal control officer under this chapter. The Mayor and City Council may appoint additional person or persons, as it deems necessary and proper to act as animal control officer, who shall be under the supervision and control of the Chief of Police, and who shall be responsible for the enforcement of all animal control regulations. The compensation to such person or persons shall be determined from time to time by the City Council. (Ord. 699, 2-18-1997; amd. Ord. 939, 11-18-2019) **6-2-7: IMPOUNDMENT OF DOGS AND OTHER ANIMALS:** All dogs/animals found running at large within the City limits in violation of this Chapter, may be impounded by the animal control officer, whether such dog/animal is owned/harbored by a person residing within the City limits, or elsewhere. When any dog bearing a license tag, is impounded by the animal control officer, the animal control officer shall notify the owner/harborer of the impoundment. The owner/harborer may recover possession of such dog upon payment to the City of the fees and costs as established in the master fee schedule. If the owner/harborer of any dog impounded, fails to pay the fees prescribed, within five (5) days of the impoundment, the animal control officer may dispose of the dog/animal. It shall be the duty of the animal control officer, to post on the entrance to the police department printed notices describing the dog, by sex, color, markings, and breed if it can be determined, of all dogs impounded by the City. All other animals impounded by the animal control officer will be disposed of as provided by Idaho Code. (Ord. 699, 2-18-1997; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018; Ord. 939, 11-18-2019) **6-2-8: VIOLATIONS AND REMEDIES CUMULATIVE:** The violations, punishments, and remedies provided in this Chapter shall be cumulative with other provisions of the Grangeville City Code, State and Federal laws. The City may cause any conduct or condition in violation of this Chapter constituting a public nuisance to be abated as a public nuisance in the manner provided by law. (Ord. 699, 2-18-1997; amd. Ord. 939, 11-18-2019) **6-2-9: PENALTY FOR VIOLATION:** Except for Section 6-2-3, subsections E, J, K, M, N, O, and Q, for which the penalty shall be a regular misdemeanor penalty under Idaho State law, the remaining violations under this Chapter shall be punished as follows: A. Upon conviction of up to three (3) offenses, fines are as established in the master fee schedule; B. Upon conviction for a fourth offense, involving the same animal and/or the same owner, the animal shall be ordered destroyed in a humane manner by the animal control officer. (Ord. 897, 3-2-2015; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018; Ord. 939, 11-18-2019)

laws.title: Curfew
laws.content:
**SECTION:**

6-3-1: Definitions

6-3-2: Prohibited Hours

6-3-3: Responsibility Of Parents And/Or Guardians

6-3-4: Presumption Of Presence On Street

**6-3-1: DEFINITIONS:**

Unless specifically defined below, words or phrases used in this Chapter shall be interpreted so as to give them the meaning they have in common usage and to give this Chapter its most reasonable application:

**LEGAL GUARDIAN:** Any person, male or female, eighteen (18) years of age or older having the legal custody of a minor.

**LEGAL PARENT/PARENTS:** Biological or legal adoptive mother and father or any combination thereof.

**MINOR:** Any person, male or female, seventeen (17) years of age or under.

**OTHER:** Any person, male or female, eighteen (18) years of age or older having the temporary custody of any minor in the absence of the legal parent(s) or legal guardian. (Ord. 665, 6-6-1994)

**6-3-2: PROHIBITED HOURS:**

It shall be unlawful and an infraction for any minor to be in any public place or to be upon any street, alley or public grounds within the City between the hours of ten thirty o’clock (10:30) P.M. and five o’clock (5:00) A.M. on the nights of Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, and between the hours of twelve o’clock (12:00) midnight and five o’clock (5:00) A.M. on Friday and Saturday except under the following conditions:

A. In attendance at or going to or from a recognized school function.

B. In attendance at or going to or from a supervised public, fraternal or church activity.

C. With written permission from a parent or legal guardian for a specific purpose, and only for a specific date and time. Any blanket permission shall be considered as being no permission.

D. Any proven emergency situation.

E. When accompanied by parent(s) or legal guardian.

(Ord. 665, 6-6-1994; amd. Ord. 975, 7-1-2024)

**6-3-3: RESPONSIBILITY OF PARENTS AND/OR GUARDIANS:**

Any parent, parents, legal guardian or other adult persons having custody or control of any minor or minors, as defined in Section 6-3-1 hereof, permitting, allowing or abetting said minor or minors to violate Section 6-3-2 hereof on a second or subsequent occasion shall be deemed guilty of a violation of the Juvenile Corrections Act relating to “encouraging violations”, Idaho Code 20-526, and the finding that said minor or minors have violated said section for a second or subsequent time shall be presumptive proof of the encouraging of a violation of the Juvenile Corrections Act by said minor or minors.

(Ord. 665, 6-6-1994; amd. Ord. 975, 7-1-2024)

**6-3-4: PRESUMPTION OF PRESENCE ON STREET:**

A. The finding of any minor upon the streets, alleys or public places within the City during the prohibited hours without written permission or without a lawfully appearing excuse shall be prima facie showing of a violation of this Chapter, and upon such showing, any police officer shall detain said minor or minors for a reasonable time in order to notify said minor’s parent, parents, legal guardian or other adult having custody or control to pick up said minor or minors at the place of detention, and a written record, constituting a warning, shall be maintained by the Police Department.

B. Upon a second or subsequent violation of this Chapter, the parent, parents, legal guardian or other person having custody of the violating minor may be charged with the misdemeanor violation of this Chapter or the laws of the State.

(Ord. 665, 6-6-1994; amd. Ord. 975, 7-1-2024)

laws.title: Explosives
laws.content:
**SECTION:**

6-4-1: Explosives Prohibited

6-4-2: Exceptions Permitted

**6-4-1: EXPLOSIVES PROHIBITED:**

It shall be unlawful for any person to make, keep or transport any gunpowder, nitroglycerin or other highly explosive substance within the limits of the City. (Ord. 341, 7-10-1961)

**6-4-2: EXCEPTIONS PERMITTED:**

A vehicle carrying explosives may be permitted on the streets of the City, and gunpowder, nitroglycerin or other highly explosive substance may be stored within the City, only if a special written permit has first been obtained from the Chief of Police; such permit shall specify the exact route to be used by said vehicle and may permit the vehicle to be parked at a certain specified place for a certain specified period of time; and such permit for storage shall specify the exact place of storage and shall impose other reasonable regulations for the protection of the public safety and welfare. Each such permit shall be valid only for the one specified use expressed therein. (Ord. 341, 7-10-1961)

laws.title: Fireworks
laws.content:
**SECTION:**

6-5-1: Title

6-5-2: Definitions

6-5-3: Application To Display Fireworks

6-5-4: Application Approval

6-5-5: Investigation Of Application, Findings

6-5-6: Investigation Of Application, Approval Or Denial

6-5-7: Special Permit, Proof Of Compensation Insurance

6-5-8: Signed Application

6-5-9: Labeling Of Fireworks As To Type
6-5-10: Sale Of Safe Fireworks, Packaging

6-5-11: Right To Sell Safe Fireworks

6-5-12: Fireworks Must Be Labeled Before Transfer Allowed

6-5-13: Exemptions From Chapter

6-5-14: Rockets And Missiles Exempted

6-5-15: Permit Fee

6-5-16: Penalty

6-5-1: TITLE:

This Chapter shall be known and may be cited as the City of Grangeville Fireworks Ordinance. (Ord. 418, 4-5-1971)

6-5-2: DEFINITIONS:

The definitions set forth in this Chapter shall govern the construction of this Chapter, unless the context otherwise requires.

AGRICULTURAL AND WILDLIFE FIREWORKS: Includes fireworks designated or used to prevent damage to crops or unwanted occupancy of areas by animals or birds through the employment of sound or light, or both, whenever such fireworks are so classified.

DANGEROUS FIREWORKS: Includes any of the following:

A. Firecrackers, cannon crackers, giant crackers, salutes, silver tube salutes, cherry bombs, mines, ground bombardment, grasshoppers and other explosive articles of similar nature;

B. Blank cartridges;

C. Sky rockets and rockets, including all similar devices employing any combustible or explosive material and which rise in the air during discharge;

D. Roman candles, including all devices which discharge balls of fire into the air;

E. Chasers and whistles, including all devices which dart or travel about the surface of the ground during discharge;

F. Snakes and hats containing bichloride of mercury;

G. Sparklers more than ten inches (10") in length or one-quarter inch ( $\frac{1}{4}$ ") in diameter;

H. All articles for pyrotechnic display such as aerial shells, salutes, flash shells, sky battles, parachute shells, mines, Dago bombs and similar devices;

I. All torpedoes which explode by means of friction, or which contain arsenic, and all other similar fireworks devices including cracker balls;

J. Fire balloons or balloons of any type which have burning material of any kind attached thereto.

FIRE NUISANCE: Anything or any act which increases, or may cause an increase of, the hazard or menace of fire to a greater degree than customarily recognized as normal by persons in the public service of preventing, suppressing, or extinguishing fire; or which may obstruct, delay, or hinder, or may become the cause of any obstruction, delay, or a hindrance to the prevention or extinguishment of fire.

FIREWORKS: Those "common" and/or "special" fireworks devices primarily designed to produce a visible or audible effect by combustion, deflagration, explosion or detonation.

FIREWORKS PACKAGE: Includes any case, container, or receptacle used for holding fireworks, which shall be closed or sealed by tape, cordage, or by any other secure means.

PERSON: Includes any individual, firm, partnership, joint adventure, association, concern, corporation, estate, trust, business trust, receiver, syndicate or any other group or combination acting as a unit.

PUBLIC DISPLAY OF FIREWORKS: An entertainment feature where the public is admitted or permitted to view the display or discharge of dangerous fireworks.

SAFE AND SANE FIREWORKS: Includes any of the following:

A. Cone fountains with pyrotechnic composition not exceeding fifty (50) grams each;

B. Cylindrical fountains, whether base, spike or handle, with pyrotechnic composition not exceeding seventy five (75) grams each and inside tube diameter not exceeding three-quarters inch ( $\frac{3}{4}$ ");

C. Sparklers and "dipped sticks" not more than ten inches (10") in length or one-quarter inch ( $\frac{1}{4}$ ") in diameter and Suzuki and Morning Glories with pyrotechnic composition not exceeding four (4) grams each;

D. Snakes which do not contain bichloride of mercury and pyrotechnic composition not exceeding two (2) grams each;

E. Wheels with pyrotechnic composition not exceeding sixty (60) grains for each driver unit or two hundred forty (240) grains for each complete wheel. The inside tube diameter of driver unit shall not exceed one-half inch ( $\frac{1}{2}$ ");

F. Whistles, without report and which do not dart or travel about the ground during discharge with pyrotechnic composition not exceeding six (6) grams and containing not picric or gallic acid.

TYPES OF FIREWORKS, EXEMPTIONS: Fireworks shall include blank cartridges, toy pistols, toy cannon, toy canes or toy guns in which explosives are used, fire balloons (balloons of a type which have burning material of any kind attached thereto or which require fire underneath to propel them), firecrackers, torpedoes, skyrockets, rockets, Roman candles, fountains, wheels, Dago bombs, sparklers, and other fireworks of like construction and any fireworks containing any combustible or explosive substance for the purpose of producing a visible or audible effect by combustion, deflagration, explosion or detonation.

Exempted from this part are all toy pistols, toy cannons, toy canes and toy guns and similar devices such as party poppers or party favors in which paper caps containing not more than twenty-five hundredths (.25) grain of explosive compound per cap are used and such caps whether single, roll or tape type. (Ord. 418, 4-5-1971)

6-5-3: APPLICATION TO DISPLAY FIREWORKS:

Any adult person or other group desiring to make a public display of fireworks, or use, or discharge agricultural or wildlife fireworks, shall first make written application to the Chief of the Fire Department of the City. (Ord. 418, 4-5-1971)

6-5-4: APPLICATION APPROVAL:

The governing body of the City shall have power in its discretion to grant or deny the application, subject to such reasonable conditions, if any, as it shall prescribe. (Ord. 418, 4-5-1971)

6-5-5: INVESTIGATION OF APPLICATION, FINDINGS:

It shall be the duty of the City Fire Chief to whom the application for a permit was made to make an investigation and submit a report of his findings and his recommendation for or against the issuance of the permit, together with his reasons therefor, to the governing body of the City. (Ord. 418, 4-5-1971)

6-5-6: INVESTIGATION OF APPLICATION, APPROVAL OR DENIAL:

It shall be the duty of the City Fire Chief, to whom the application for a permit for a public display of fireworks is made, to make an investigation as to whether such a display as proposed will be of such character and will be so located that it may be hazardous to property or dangerous to any person, and that each person assisting in such display is fully qualified by training to properly handle such display without danger to themselves or to the public, and he shall, in the exercise of reasonable discretion, grant or deny the application, subject to such reasonable conditions, if any, as he may prescribe. (Ord. 418, 4-5-1971)

6-5-7: SPECIAL PERMIT, PROOF OF COMPENSATION INSURANCE:

The City Fire Chief or City Council may require the applicant for a special permit for a public fireworks display or the use or discharge of agricultural or wildlife fireworks at the time of application to furnish proof that he carries compensation insurance for his employees as provided by the laws of the State of Idaho, and adequate public liability and property damage insurance. (Ord. 418, 4-5-1971)

6-5-8: SIGNED APPLICATION:

The application for a license shall be signed by the applicant. If application is made by a partnership, it shall be signed by each partner of the partnership, and if application is made by a corporation, it shall be signed by an officer of the corporation and bear the seal of the corporation. (Ord. 418, 4-5-1971)

6-5-9: LABELING OF FIREWORKS AS TO TYPE:

The manufacturer, importer or wholesaler shall stamp or label each case or carton of fireworks offered for sale, sold, consigned or delivered within the City, for sale or use within the City, as dangerous fireworks, safe and sane fireworks, or agricultural or wildlife fireworks, and branded as required by public law 89-756, 89th Congress, S.3298, November 3, 1966. (Ord. 418, 4-5-1971)

6-5-10: SALE OF SAFE FIREWORKS, PACKAGING:

No safe and sane fireworks shall be sold or offered for sale at retail unless the fuses or other igniting devices are protected by a approved protective caps or each item or group of items is enclosed or sealed in a package bearing such brand and label. (Ord. 418, 4-5-1971)

6-5-11: RIGHT TO SELL SAFE FIREWORKS:

Safe and sane fireworks shall not be sold or offered for sale at retail, given away, or discharged except from twelve o'clock (12:00) noon, on June 29, to twelve o'clock (12:00) midnight on July 5, of each year.

Dangerous fireworks shall not be sold at retail, given away, possessed or discharged except to a person having a valid license for public display, or agricultural and wildlife use and defined by the Idaho laws issued by the City Council. It shall be the duty of every seller or distributor of dangerous fireworks to require each licensee to present said license to the seller or distributor of dangerous fireworks at the time of every sale to the licensed person. No dangerous fireworks shall be discharged or used except for public display, or for agricultural and wildlife use, pursuant to a license therefor.

A violation of these provisions shall be a misdemeanor and punishable as hereinafter set forth. (Ord. 418, 4-5-1971)
6-5-12: FIREWORKS MUST BE LABELED BEFORE TRANSFER ALLOWED:

The transfer of dangerous fireworks or agricultural or wildlife fireworks or safe and sane fireworks ownership, whether by sale at wholesale or retail, by gift or other means of conveyance of title or the delivery of any fireworks to any person in the City, which is not labeled and branded as required by the Federal law above noted, is prohibited. (Ord. 418, 4-5-1971)

6-5-13: EXEMPTIONS FROM CHAPTER:

This chapter does not prohibit:

A. Any manufacturer, wholesaler, or retailer from selling blank cartridges for use by persons for bona fide ceremonial purposes, athletic or sports events, or military ceremonials or demonstrations and theatrical or motion picture productions;

B. The use of torpedoes, flares, or fuses (fusees) by motor vehicles, railroads, or other transportation agencies for signal purposes of illumination or for use in forest protection activities; or

C. The assembling, compounding, use and display of fireworks of whatever nature by any person engaged in the production of motion pictures, theatricals, or operas when such use and display is a necessary part of the production and such person possesses a valid permit to purchase, possess, transport or use dangerous fireworks. (Ord. 418, 4-5-1971)

6-5-14: ROCKETS AND MISSILES EXEMPTED:

The provisions of this chapter do not apply to research or experiments with rockets or missiles, or the production, transportation, or firing of rockets or missiles, by the Department of Defense of the United States, or by any agency or organization acting pursuant to its contract which it has with the Department of Defense for the development or production of rockets or missiles. (Ord. 418, 4-5-1971)

6-5-15: PERMIT FEE:

A permit fee shall be payable to the City Clerk by any licensee hereunder, in the amount as established in the master fee schedule. (Ord. 418, 4-5-1971; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018)

6-5-16: PENALTY:

A. The unlawful possession of any class or kind of fireworks in violation of the provisions of this chapter shall be a misdemeanor and punishable as hereinafter provided. (Ord. 418, 4-5-1971)

B. Any person violating any of the provisions of this chapter or any rules or regulations issued thereunder, is guilty of a misdemeanor, and shall be punishable by a fine as established in the master fee schedule or by imprisonment in the Municipal Jail for not more than thirty (30) days, or by both such fine and imprisonment. (Ord. 418, 4-5-1971; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018)

**CHAPTER 6**

**ABANDONED, WRECKED VEHICLES**

SECTION:

6-6-1: Accumulation Unlawful

6-6-2: Definition

6-6-3: Junk On Residential Or Business Property

6-6-4: Exemptions

6-6-5: Removal

6-6-6: Notice

6-6-7: Failure To Remove

6-6-8: Enforcement

6-6-9: Abatement

6-6-10: Expenses To Be Paid By Creating Party

6-6-1: ACCUMULATION UNLAWFUL:

The accumulation and storage of abandoned, wrecked, dismantled or inoperative vehicles or parts thereof or other junked or abandoned personal property on private or public property in the City and adjacent thereto within a distance of one-quarter ($^{1/4}$) mile of the City limits is hereby found to create a condition tending to reduce the value of private property, to promote blight and deterioration, to invite plundering, to create fire hazards, to constitute an attractive nuisance creating a hazard to health and safety of minors, to create a harborage for rodents and insects and to be injurious to the health, safety and general welfare of the residents of the City and of the adjacent area. Therefore, the presence of such abandoned or junked items on private or public property in the City and within one-quarter ($^{1/4}$) mile of the City limits, except as expressly hereinafter permitted, is hereby declared to constitute a public nuisance which may be abated as such in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter. (Ord. 411, 7-8-1970)

6-6-2: DEFINITION:

An abandoned, wrecked, dismantled or inoperative motor vehicle, or part thereof, hereinafter called a junk vehicle, shall be defined as an unsightly motor vehicle or a part or parts therefrom, which meets any one of the following qualifications:

A. It does not carry a current valid State registration and license plates.

B. It cannot be safely operated under its own power.

C. It is not in a garage or other building.

D. It does not have any one of the following: foot brakes, hand brakes, headlights, tail lights, horn, muffler, rearview mirror, windshield wipers, or adequate fenders. (Ord. 411, 7-8-1970)

6-6-3: JUNK ON RESIDENTIAL OR BUSINESS PROPERTY:

It shall be unlawful for any person to maintain a junk vehicle, vehicles, or parts thereof, or junked or abandoned furniture, appliances, trailers, campers or other similar junked or abandoned articles or materials, on residential property or business property exposed to the public view for a period of more than thirty (30) days. (Ord. 411, 7-8-1970)

6-6-4: EXEMPTIONS:

This Chapter shall not apply to:

A. A vehicle or part thereof or other personal property which is completely enclosed within a building in a lawful manner where it is not visible from the street or other public or private property; or

B. A vehicle or personal property which is stored or parked in a lawful manner on private property in connection with the business of a licensed dismantler, licensed vehicle dealer, a junk dealer, or when such storage or parking is necessary to the operation of a lawfully conducted business or commercial enterprise. (Ord. 411, 7-8-1970)

6-6-5: REMOVAL:

Any member of the Police Department or Building Department may order any junk vehicle, vehicles or parts thereof, or other junked or abandoned personal property removed within ten (10) days. (Ord. 411, 7-8-1970)

6-6-6: NOTICE:

Notice of such order shall be placed upon said junk vehicle or personal property. Copies of said notice shall be served upon any adult occupying the real estate on which the junk vehicle or personal property is located and upon the owner of the junk vehicle or personal property if known. If no occupant of the real estate or owner of the junk vehicle or personal property can be found, a notice affixed to any building on the real estate shall constitute notice to the owner or occupant of the real estate and to the owner of the junk vehicle or personal property. If there is no building on the real estate said notice may be affixed elsewhere on the real estate. (Ord. 411, 7-8-1970)

6-6-7: FAILURE TO REMOVE:

It shall be unlawful and a misdemeanor for any person who is a) the owner of a junk motor vehicle or personal property, or b) the owner or occupant of the real estate on which said vehicle or personal property is situated, or c) the person who placed or abandoned said junk vehicle or personal property on such property, to fail or refuse to remove, or refuse to abate such nuisance, when ordered to do so in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter. (Ord. 411, 7-8-1970)

6-6-8: ENFORCEMENT:

It shall be unlawful and a misdemeanor to interfere with, hinder or refuse to allow any authorized City officer or employee to enter upon private or public property to enforce the provisions of this Chapter. (Ord. 411, 7-8-1970)

6-6-9: ABATEMENT:

If said junk vehicle or other junked or abandoned personal property is not removed within the time so fixed, the Police Department may cause said junk vehicle or personal property to be removed at the expense of the owner and placed in an impounded yard where they shall be offered for sale to the highest and best bidder at public auction to be held not later than ten (10) days after one publication and notice of such sale to be published in a local newspaper. The proceeds from such sale shall be used to pay towing or removal expenses and rental in impounded yard where said junk vehicles are held. In the event the sale of the impounded junk vehicle or other personal property fails to produce enough revenue to pay the towing and impounding charges the balance will be due and payable immediately by the owner of the personal property, or the owner of the property where the personal property was located.

The Police Department may, however, dispose of any junked vehicle or other junked or abandoned personal property after notice and removal of the same as hereinbefore provided, without necessity of notice of sale and public auction when said personal property does not have market or salvage value of more than ten dollars ($10.00). (Ord. 411, 7-8-1970)

6-6-10: EXPENSES TO BE PAID BY CREATING PARTY:

In addition to the authority granted by this Chapter, under Idaho Code 50-334, the City is empowered to prevent, remove and abate said nuisances at the expenses of the parties creating, causing, committing or maintaining the same, and the City may levy a special assessment as provided in Idaho Code 50-1008 on the land or premises whereon the nuisance is situated to defray the cost or to reimburse the City for the cost of abating the same. (Ord. 411, 7-8-1970)

laws.title: Camping
laws.content:
**SECTION:** 6-7-1: Title 6-7-2: Definitions 6-7-3: Camping On Public Property Prohibited 6-7-4: Special Camping Zones And Camping On Leased City Property 6-7-5: Violations; Public Nuisance; Other City Remedies Preserved 6-7-6: Additional Provisions 6-7-1: TITLE: This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the City of Grangeville camping ordinance. (Ord. 982, 7-7-2025) 6-7-2: DEFINITIONS: The definitions set forth in this chapter shall govern the construction of this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires. As used in this chapter, the following terms shall have the following meanings:
CAMP AND CAMPING: The use or occupancy of any public property as a temporary or permanent place of residence, lodging, dwelling, habitation or abode, whether or not such conduct occurs within or outside of any temporary or permanent structure, shelter, other enclosure or vehicle of any kind or nature. Prima facie evidence of camping may include, but is not limited to, storage of personal belongings, using tents or other temporary structures, shelters or enclosures for sleeping or storage of personal belongings, carrying on cooking activities or making any fire in an unauthorized area, or any of these activities in combination with one another or in combination with either sleeping or making preparations to sleep (including the laying down of bedding for the purpose of sleeping).
CITY PROPERTY: A. Any and all real property owned by the city, whether inside or outside of city limits, including but not limited to any city park, playground, ball field, sports field, recreational field, ski hill, or parking lot, and
B. Any and all city streets, sidewalks, alleys and rights of way within the city.
PUBLIC PROPERTY: A. Any and all city property, and
B. Any and all public streets, sidewalks, alleys and rights of way within the city. (Ord. 982, 7-7-2025)
6-7-3: CAMPING ON PUBLIC PROPERTY PROHIBITED: Unless otherwise provided under this chapter or authorized by the city or by law, it is unlawful for any person to camp upon or within any public property or any portion thereof. (Ord. 982, 7-7-2025) 6-7-4: SPECIAL CAMPING ZONES AND CAMPING ON LEASED CITY PROPERTY: The city council may by resolution designate any portion of any city property as a “special camping zone” authorizing temporary camping upon or within said city property for events or activities such as sporting or school events, on such terms and conditions as the city council deems in the best interest of the city. Such a resolution shall describe the portion of city property included in the special camping zone and specify the inclusive dates and times during which camping within the zone are permitted. Any such designated camping zones shall be marked with signage identifying the city property included in the zone and the inclusive dates and times during which camping within the zone is permitted. It shall be unlawful for any person camping within any designated special camping zone to knowingly a) violate any term or condition of the special camping zone designation established by the city council, or b) refuse or otherwise fail to vacate and cease camping within said any designated special camping zone upon expiration or earlier termination of the special camping zone designation. The city council may by resolution from time to time amend or terminate any special camping zone designation made by the city council under this section as the city council deems it in the best interest of the city. Any camping on city property leased to a third party shall be at the discretion and control of the third party, subject to the terms of the lease and any applicable laws. (Ord. 982, 7-7-2025) 6-7-5: VIOLATIONS; PUBLIC NUISANCE; OTHER CITY REMEDIES PRESERVED: A. Every person who pleads guilty to or is found guilty of violating any provision of this chapter is guilty of a misdemeanor. B. Any violation of this chapter shall be punishable by incarceration in the county jail up to six (6) months, or a fine as established in the master fee schedule, or both said jail and fine. C. Any violation of this chapter is hereby also declared to be a public nuisance. The city may also pursue all other and further remedies provided by this code or otherwise provided by law against any person who has violated or is violating any provision of this chapter, including but not limited to as provided under trespass laws and nuisance laws, with all remedies of city being cumulative and non-exclusive. (Ord. 982, 7-7-2025) 6-7-6: ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS: This chapter supplements and does not supersede nor revoke in whole or in part any other applicable federal, state, county or city laws, regulations, codes or ordinances regulating, prohibiting, or restricting camping, sleeping, dwelling or parking upon any public street, sidewalk, alley, right of way or any other public property. (Ord. 982, 7-7-2025)

laws.title: Burning Restrictions
Inspection
laws.content: The city inspector, any peace officer, or health officer of the state, the county, and the city, shall have the right to go upon any premises during reasonable hours for the purpose of inspecting all places and containers where rubbish and/or garbage is accumulated or kept. (Ord. 404, 5-5-1969, eff. 6-1-1969)

laws.title: Licensing and Contracting
laws.content: The mayor and city council shall be the sole authority to license, contract for or to otherwise provide for all services pertaining to sanitary collection and disposal within the city, let bids for or establish reasonable fees for licenses or franchises and is hereby authorized to enter into contracts with one or more contractors, and establish reasonable rules and regulations governing the conduct and operation of such licensees or contractors. The city council may require of any licensee or contractor a bond in a reasonable amount, the condition of which shall be satisfactory performance of the contract. (Ord. 404, 5-5-1969, eff. 6-1-1969)

laws.title: Solid Waste Disposal Prohibited
laws.content:
A. It shall be unlawful for any person to incinerate solid waste or to deposit the same on vacant lots or private property. No person, including the contractor, shall drop, spill or permit solid waste to fall upon any private property, public street, alley or right of way without immediately cleaning up said waste.

B. After emptying any container (except bags), contractor’s employees shall return containers to the location in which such containers were taken, and shall replace the covers. Space about the containers shall be left free from any solid waste spilled during the collection. The contractor is not responsible for cleaning up conditions about solid waste containers caused by the carelessness of the owner or others. (Ord. 612, 2-6-1989)

laws.title: Theft
laws.content:
A. Theft Of Services:

1. It shall be unlawful for any person to deposit solid waste in any commercial container placed for a private or public individual, business, or agency unless the person has been so authorized by the owner or individual in charge of the container.

2. It shall be unlawful for any person not a resident of the City to leave solid waste with a City resident for pick up pursuant to this chapter.

3. Violation of this subsection shall be construed as a theft of services. (Ord. 612, 2-6-1989)

B. Theft Of Solid Waste: It shall be unlawful for any person to enter into, to search in, or to remove any solid waste of any kind or description including, but not limited to, recyclables which have been deposited in solid waste refuse containers, including dumpsters within the City, if the containers are open to use by the public.

No person shall be convicted of violating this subsection if that person possesses advance written permission to engage in any of the aforementioned acts. Such permission must be signed by an authorized agent of the Grangeville solid waste contractor. (Ord. 700, 6-16-1997)

laws.title: Suppression of Nuisances
laws.content:
A. The Public Works Director shall take cognizance of all solid waste related nuisances within the limits of the jurisdiction of the City, and shall take such measures as may be effectual to suppress and abate the same, including contracting to abate such nuisance and billing the property owner for the expense of abatement.

B. The improper collection, disposal or discharge into the atmosphere of hazardous material is hereby declared to be a nuisance and is unlawful. (Ord. 612, 2-6-1989)

laws.title: Penalties
laws.content: Any person violating any of the provisions of this chapter shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and upon conviction thereof be fined in an amount as established in the master fee schedule or be imprisoned in the Idaho County Jail for a period of not to exceed six (6) months or both. Each day such violation is committed or permitted to continue and/or each separate incident shall constitute a separate offense and be punishable as described hereunder. (Ord. 841, 8-4-2008; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018)

laws.title: Rates
laws.content:
A. The City after the effective date hereof shall reserve the right to amend residential rate structures for garbage service. (Ord. 775, 9-20-2004; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018)

B. By the adoption of section 7-1-13 of this chapter, the City has made mandatory the use of ninety five (95) gallon residential mechanical carts within the City for all solid waste except for "yard waste" as otherwise defined in this chapter. Therefore, it shall be the rate that each residence shall pay the amount established in the master fee schedule. Residential mechanical containers, also known as carts, in excess of one per residence shall pay an additional fee as established in the master fee schedule. If more than four (4) carts are used the residential user will be required to
subscribe to a commercial container of two (2) yards in capacity or bigger. (Ord. 775, 9-20-2004; amd. Res. 226, 9-6-2011; Res. 229, 9-4-2012; Res. 254, 9-5-2017; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018)

C. Additionally, the residential mechanical cart may be used for commercial businesses which produce limited amounts of solid waste. For commercial establishments the fee for carts will be as established in the master fee schedule, up to a maximum of four (4) carts at which time that commercial user will be required to subscribe to a commercial container of two (2) yards in capacity or larger.

D. The City hereby reserves the right to ratify and approve the commercial rate structure as the same shall be agreed upon between the contractor and any commercial user in the future. The commercial rate structure adopted in ordinance 612 or the commercial rate for the use of residential mechanical containers/carts shall be as described in this section. Those rates shall remain in place until they are amended. New commercial rate structures may not be adopted unless the contract shall provide for such amended rate structures to the City Clerk as shall be agreed upon between the contractor and such commercial users. The provisions of subsection 7-1-3D of this chapter relating to the City’s power to regulate maximum rates shall remain unimpaired by the adoption of this section.

E. The City Clerk shall maintain in her office, open to public inspection, copies of all rate schedules and make the same available to members of the public upon inquiry. (Ord. 775, 9-20-2004; amd. Ord. 925, 10-1-2018)

laws.title: Refuse in Buildings
laws.content:
SECTION:

7-2-1: Refuse In Buildings; Stagnant Water

7-2-1: REFUSE IN BUILDINGS; STAGNANT WATER:

It shall be unlawful for any person to permit or suffer to be in or accumulate in, or upon any yard, lot, place or premises or upon any street or sidewalk adjacent to or abutting upon any lot, block, place or premises or in any building or shed owned or occupied by him or for which he may be agent within the limits of the Municipality, any stagnant water or impure water, refuse, vegetable decay or decaying substance, garbage or filth of any kind, nor suffer such yard, lot, place, building or premises to be or to remain in such condition as to cause or create a nuisance or offensive smell or to pollute or render unhealthful the atmosphere or the premises or thereby to be, become, cause or create a public nuisance. (1959 Code)
